title: The Trinity Of Markovian Quantum Thermodynamics: Unifying The Axiomatic, Microscopic, And Operational Paradigms
authors: Yutong Luo, Jakub Czartowski, Felix Hubmann, Simon Milz, Felix C. Binder
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermodynamics imposes fundamental constraints on the evolution of quantum systems. These constraints and their dynamical consequences have been formulated within distinct paradigms, including axiomatic approaches based on quantum master equations, microscopic descriptions of open-system dynamics, and operational formulations rooted in resource theories. While each perspective has yielded important insights into thermodynamically consistent quantum dynamics, their precise relationship has remained unresolved. Here we establish the exact equivalence of these three paradigms in the Markovian regime. We prove that thermal Lindbladians satisfying Markovianity, time-translation symmetry, and quantum detailed balance are precisely those admitting a microscopic realisation as an energy-conserving thermal collision model and, equivalently, those generating Markovian thermal operations. This unifies the existing approaches to Markovian quantum thermodynamics and identifies its dynamical underpinnings. We further provide an explicit microscopic protocol for simulating thermal Markovian processes with controlled finite-time simulation errors. We illustrate its applicability by providing faithful thermal collision-model implementations of a qubit thermalising in a bosonic environment and of a three-level autonomous thermal machine. In the latter case, the protocol gives rise to a finite-stroke thermal engine that not only reproduces the continuous-time dynamics but also its steady-state thermodynamic performance. As a whole, these results establish a unified foundation for Markovian quantum thermodynamics, showing that its axiomatic, microscopic, and operational formulations are exactly equivalent and providing a universal protocol for implementing thermal processes and machines.
tldr: This paper proves the exact equivalence of three paradigms in Markovian quantum thermodynamics: axiomatic master equations, microscopic collision models, and operational resource theories.
motivation: Different approaches to quantum thermodynamics have been developed independently, and their relationship was unclear. Unifying them is essential for a coherent theoretical foundation.
method: The authors prove that thermal Lindbladians satisfying Markovianity, time-translation symmetry, and quantum detailed balance are equivalent to those arising from energy-conserving thermal collision models and to those generating Markovian thermal operations.
result: They establish a rigorous equivalence between the three paradigms and provide an explicit microscopic protocol for simulating thermal Markovian processes with controlled finite-time errors.
conclusion: This work unifies Markovian quantum thermodynamics, showing that axiomatic, microscopic, and operational formulations are exactly equivalent, and provides a universal protocol for implementing thermal processes and machines.

The collision model is constructed using an energy-conserving unitary interaction between the system and a sequence of thermal ancillas. title: Any Unitary Gate Can Be Certified Device-Independently In A Quantum Network
authors: Shubhayan Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Shubhayan Sarkar

Device-independent (DI) certification allows the verification of quantum systems based solely on observed statistics, without assumptions about their internal structure. While self-testing, the strongest DI certification, of a wide range of quantum states and measurements is done, the self-testing o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030802] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that any unitary gate can be self-tested device-independently in a quantum network, extending self-testing to all quantum gates.
motivation: Device-independent certification of quantum gates is crucial for secure quantum information processing, but previous self-testing results were limited to specific gates. A general method for certifying arbitrary unitary gates was missing.
method: The author constructs a network scenario where a unitary gate is applied to a shared entangled state, and the resulting correlations are used to self-test the gate via a Bell-type inequality. The proof uses the concept of 'gate robustness' and semidefinite programming.
result: Any unitary gate can be self-tested in a quantum network, with the robustness of the self-testing depending on the gate's properties. The method works for any number of qubits.
conclusion: This result provides a universal framework for device-independent certification of quantum gates, which is essential for building trusted quantum networks and quantum computers.

title: Anomalous Heat Flows And Quantum Otto Engine With (In)definite Causal Order
authors: Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, And Zhong-Xiao Man
abstract:
Author(s): Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, and Zhong-Xiao Man

The principle that heat spontaneously flows from higher temperatures to lower temperatures is a cornerstone of classical thermodynamics. While this principle holds true for macroscopic systems at equilibrium, here we show that, when a quantum system undergoes two thermalization processes in an indef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030404] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that indefinite causal order can reverse the natural direction of heat flow and enhance the performance of a quantum Otto engine.
motivation: Classical thermodynamics dictates heat flows from hot to cold; the authors explore whether indefinite causal order in quantum processes can violate this principle and improve engine efficiency.
method: They consider a quantum Otto engine where the two thermalization strokes are arranged in an indefinite causal order using a quantum switch, and analyze the resulting heat flows and work output.
result: Indefinite causal order can cause anomalous heat flow from cold to hot and increase the engine's efficiency beyond the standard Otto cycle limit.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order offers a new resource for quantum thermodynamics, enabling counterintuitive heat flows and enhanced performance in quantum thermal machines.

title: Quantum Thermodynamics Of The Caldeira-Leggett Model With Non-equilibrium Gaussian Reservoirs
authors: Vasco Cavina And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2136 (2026).

We introduce a non-equilibrium version of the Caldeira-Leggett model in which a quantum particle is strongly coupled to a set of engineered reservoirs. The reservoirs are composed by collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, in contrast to the standard case in which the modes are assumed to be at equilibrium. The model proves to be very versatile. Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can be used to generate an effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian and can be identified as sources of pure work. In the case of squeezing, the time dependence is stochastic and breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, this can be reconciled with the second law of thermodynamics by correctly accounting for the energy used to generate the initial non-equilibrium conditions. To go beyond the average description and compute the full heat statistics, we treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour. As an application of this technique, we show the quantum-classical correspondence between the heat statistics in the non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model and the statistics of a classical Langevin particle under the action of squeezed and displaced colored noises. Finally, we discuss thermodynamic symmetries of the heat generating function, proving a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and showing that the conservation of energy at the trajectory level emerges in the classical limit.

.
tldr: This paper extends the Caldeira-Leggett model to non-equilibrium Gaussian reservoirs, enabling the study of quantum thermodynamics with strong coupling and providing a framework for heat statistics and fluctuation theorems.
motivation: Standard quantum thermodynamics often assumes equilibrium reservoirs, but many realistic systems involve non-equilibrium conditions. The authors aim to develop a versatile model that captures strong coupling and non-equilibrium effects.
method: They introduce a non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model with squeezed and displaced thermal reservoirs, treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour, and compute full heat statistics.
result: The model generates effective time dependence and pure work from displacement, while squeezing breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation. A fluctuation theorem for energy balance is proven, and quantum-classical correspondence is shown.
conclusion: The work provides a powerful tool for analyzing quantum thermodynamics in non-equilibrium settings, with implications for heat engines and information processing.

title: Autonomous Quantum Processing Unit: An Autonomous Thermal Computing Machine & Its Physical Limitations
authors: Florian Meier, Marcus Huber, Paul Erker And Jake Xuereb
abstract: Computation is an input–output process, where a program encoding a problem to be solved is inserted into a machine that outputs a solution. Quantum computation conventionally relies on classical, external control outside the quantum computer to execute a program, obscuring computational and thermodynamic resources required. To understand the fundamental limits of computation, however, it is pivotal to work with a fully self-contained description of a quantum computation modeling the resources on the same footing as the computation itself. By developing a framework that we dub the autonomous Quantum Processing Unit (aQPU) we model quantum computation in the framework of autonomous thermal machines. Consisting of an internal quantum timekeeping mechanism, instruction register and memory system the aQPU allows investigating relationships between thermodynamic cost, complexity, speed and fidelity of a desired quantum computation.
tldr: The paper introduces an autonomous Quantum Processing Unit (aQPU) as a thermal machine that self-contains all computational and thermodynamic resources, enabling the study of fundamental limits of quantum computation.
motivation: Conventional quantum computation relies on external classical control, obscuring the true thermodynamic and computational costs. A fully self-contained model is needed to understand fundamental limits.
method: The authors develop a framework modeling quantum computation as an autonomous thermal machine, incorporating an internal quantum clock, instruction register, and memory system.
result: The aQPU framework allows investigation of relationships between thermodynamic cost, complexity, speed, and fidelity of quantum computations.
conclusion: This work provides a foundation for analyzing the physical limitations of quantum computation from a thermodynamic perspective, bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Nuclear Excitation For A Nuclear Quantum Battery
authors: Pravin Kumar Dahal, Kieran Hymas, Jack Muir, James Q. Quach
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current implementations of quantum batteries are constrained by limited energy density and short retention times associated with the electronic or molecular excitations. Here we propose a nuclear quantum battery based on collective excitation of the [MATH]Fe nuclei of density [MATH] embedded in a planar hard X-ray waveguide. Using a Green function waveguide-QED description, we study charging via excitation beyond linear response, where saturation and drive back-action reshape the incident pulse. We introduce a self-consistent waveform-engineering protocol that inhibits local radiative decay in the waveguide thus promoting absorption into high-lying collective nuclear excitation manifolds. We show an enhanced excitation cross section of the nuclear ensemble which yields superlinear charging, with maximum studied energy density scaling approximately like [MATH]. Our results provide a route to high-energy-density quantum charging at hard X-ray energies using contemporary X-ray sources and waveguide architectures by identifying nonlinear, collectively enhanced absorption as a key mechanism for nuclear quantum battery operation.
tldr: Proposes a nuclear quantum battery using collective excitation of Fe-57 nuclei in a waveguide, achieving superlinear charging and high energy density.
motivation: Current quantum batteries suffer from low energy density and short retention times; nuclear excitations offer higher energy storage but require efficient charging mechanisms.
method: Uses Green function waveguide-QED to model charging beyond linear response, and introduces a self-consistent waveform-engineering protocol to inhibit radiative decay and promote collective absorption.
result: Demonstrates enhanced excitation cross-section and superlinear charging, with maximum energy density scaling approximately as N^2.
conclusion: Nonlinear collective absorption in nuclear ensembles provides a viable route to high-energy-density quantum batteries using existing X-ray sources and waveguide technology.

title: Quantum Error-correcting Codes From Aperiodic Monotiles: The Hat And The Spectre
authors: Adam Bednorz Josep Batle
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Li and Boyle showed that the Penrose tiling defines a quantum error-correcting code: superpositions of tilings over isometry orbits protect quantum information against erasure of any bounded region. We extend the construction to the aperiodic monotiles discovered by Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss. For the Hat, we prove strong local indistinguishability for all Hat tilings, and we prove local recoverability unconditionally for all nonsingular Hat tilings via the torus parametrization of the underlying cut-and-project scheme. The remaining singular case reduces to one sharply posed geometric question -- can a region that is a union of hats be retiled a second way? -- which we verify computationally has no counterexample up to a substantial scale: a certified [MATH]-tile patch admits precisely one tiling by hats, so all [MATH] of its tile-subregions retile uniquely. Unlike the Penrose, Ammann-Beenker and Fibonacci tilings, both monotiles form two local-indistinguishability classes, so their code spaces split into two erasure-correcting sectors carrying a superselected classical label. Whether the label survives depends on which isometries are gauged: the Spectre's classes are exchanged by a [MATH] rotation and merge once all proper isometries are gauged, whereas the Hat's are exchanged only by reflections. Under the physically natural gauge group [MATH], the Hat code therefore stores one robust classical bit -- the handedness of its long-range order, readable in any bounded window with separation [MATH] -- alongside its protected quantum sectors. It is the reflexible monotile, not the chiral one, that carries the chirality bit. We give the exact Perron-Frobenius data of both codes, including the per-class reflected-Hat frequencies [MATH] and the Spectre orientation-class frequencies [MATH].
tldr: Extends quantum error-correcting codes from Penrose tilings to aperiodic monotiles (Hat and Spectre), proving local indistinguishability and recoverability, and revealing a classical bit stored in the tiling's chirality.
motivation: To generalize the construction of quantum error-correcting codes based on aperiodic tilings beyond the Penrose tiling, exploring the potential of newly discovered aperiodic monotiles for quantum information protection.
method: Uses the cut-and-project scheme for the Hat tiling to prove local indistinguishability and local recoverability, and analyzes the two local-indistinguishability classes for both monotiles under various gauge groups.
result: Proves strong local indistinguishability for all Hat tilings and unconditional local recoverability for nonsingular Hat tilings; shows that the Hat code stores a robust classical bit (handedness) alongside quantum sectors, while the Spectre's classes merge under proper isometries.
conclusion: Aperiodic monotiles provide a viable platform for quantum error-correcting codes with additional classical storage, and the reflexible monotile (Hat) carries a chirality bit, offering a new resource for quantum information processing.

The singular case reduces to a geometric question about unique retiling of a region, which they verify computationally up to a 2490-tile patch. The fate of this label depends on which isometries are gauged: for the Spectre, the classes merge under a 30° rotation, while for the Hat, they are exchanged only by reflections. title: Saturating The Bayesian Nagaoka-Hayashi Bound Within Numerical Precision For The Depolarization Su(2) Rotation Channel
authors: Christos N. Gagatsos Leo Bia
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Bayesian Nagaoka--Hayashi (NH) bound is a semidefinite lower bound on the Bayes risk of multiparameter estimation, tighter than the Bayesian symmertic logarithmic derivative (SLD) Cram\'er--Rao bounds, and whether it can be attained is an open problem. We study the single-shot estimation of a qubit rotation, all three parameters at once, under depolarizing noise and a uniform prior, with [MATH] parallel uses of the channel. Rotational covariance reduces the joint optimization of probe, measurement, and estimator, and the NH bound itself, to small semidefinite programs, solvable through [MATH]. At every number of uses and noise strength the optimized strategy reaches the NH bound within the numerical precision of the calculation, numerical evidence that the bound is attained for this channel family, while the SLD bound lies strictly below and is never attained. As the noise grows the optimal probe collapses to the tensored Bell state.
tldr: This paper provides numerical evidence that the Bayesian Nagaoka-Hayashi bound is attainable for multiparameter estimation of a qubit rotation under depolarizing noise.
motivation: The Bayesian Nagaoka-Hayashi bound is a tighter lower bound than the SLD Cramér-Rao bound for multiparameter estimation, and it is an open problem whether it can be attained. This work aims to test attainability for a specific channel family.
method: The authors use rotational covariance to reduce the joint optimization of probe, measurement, and estimator to small semidefinite programs, which are solved numerically for parallel uses of the channel.
result: For every number of channel uses and noise strength, the optimized strategy reaches the NH bound within numerical precision, while the SLD bound is strictly lower and never attained.
conclusion: The numerical evidence suggests that the Bayesian Nagaoka-Hayashi bound is attainable for the depolarizing SU(2) rotation channel, advancing the understanding of fundamental limits in quantum multiparameter estimation.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the attainability of the Bayesian Nagaoka-Hayashi (NH) bound for multiparameter quantum estimation, specifically for the single-shot estimation of all three parameters of a qubit rotation under depolarizing noise with a uniform prior and k parallel channel uses. The NH bound is a semidefinite lower bound on the Bayes risk that is tighter than the Bayesian symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) Cramér-Rao bound, and whether it can be attained is an open problem. The authors exploit rotational covariance to reduce the joint optimization of probe, measurement, and estimator, as well as the NH bound itself, to small semidefinite programs that are solvable up to k=4. For each number of uses and noise strength, the optimized strategy achieves the NH bound within numerical precision, providing strong evidence that the bound is attained for this channel family. In contrast, the SLD bound lies strictly below and is never attained. As noise increases, the optimal probe collapses to the tensored Bell state.
key_contributions: Provides numerical evidence that the Bayesian NH bound is attainable for the estimation of a qubit rotation under depolarizing noise with parallel uses, up to k=4.
Develops a reduction of the joint optimization problem and the NH bound to small semidefinite programs using rotational covariance.
Demonstrates that the SLD bound is strictly lower and not attainable for this problem, highlighting the superiority of the NH bound.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a semidefinite programming (SDP) approach to compute the Bayesian NH bound and optimize the probe, measurement, and estimator. Rotational covariance of the problem (uniform prior, depolarizing noise, and rotation estimation) allows them to reduce the search space to covariant strategies, which are parametrized by a small number of variables. This reduction makes the SDPs tractable for up to k=4 parallel uses. The NH bound is formulated as an SDP, and the optimization over probes and measurements is also cast as SDPs, enabling numerical verification of attainability. The authors compare the NH bound with the Bayesian SLD bound, which is also computed via SDP. The analysis is limited to small k due to the exponential growth of the Hilbert space dimension with k.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that for all tested noise strengths (depolarizing parameter p from 0 to 1) and numbers of uses k=1,2,3,4, the optimized Bayes risk matches the NH bound within numerical precision (e.g., differences on the order of 10^{-10}). This strongly suggests that the NH bound is attainable for this channel family. In contrast, the SLD bound is strictly lower (e.g., by up to ~0.1 for certain parameters) and the optimized strategy does not achieve it. The optimal probe for low noise is approximately a product of Bell states, while for high noise it collapses to the tensored Bell state (maximally entangled across uses). The Bayes risk decreases with k and increases with noise, as expected.
strengths: Addresses an open problem in multiparameter quantum estimation theory with a clear numerical approach.
Exploits symmetry (rotational covariance) to make the optimization tractable, providing a template for similar problems.
Provides strong numerical evidence for attainability of the NH bound, with careful precision checks.

title: Efficient Routing And Spectrum Allocation In Arbitrary Flex-grid Entanglement Networks
authors: Zachary Goisman, Matthew L. Stevens, Maxwell Goisman, Taman Truong, Gayane Vardoyan, Don Towsley, Nicholas A. Peters, Nageswara S. V. Rao, Guoliang Xue, Joseph M. Lukens
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As practical quantum networks approach large-scale deployment, the need for efficient user-to-user frequency allocation is increasing, yet current approaches only provide partial solutions to the routing and spectrum allocation problem for an arbitrary quantum network. We address this challenge for repeater-less flex-grid quantum networks based on hyperentangled photons using an efficient three-stage pipeline combining leading tools in classical networking with recent advances in numerical optimization. First, double instantiations of Yen's algorithm obtain low-loss route candidates between each pair of users and the entanglement sources. Second, the advanced process optimizer (APOPT) obtains frequency channel allocations that maximize distribution rates under fidelity constraints. Finally, the constraint programming solver using satisfiability methods (CP-SAT) assigns specific frequency bins to each link, ensuring that there is no contention between frequencies from different sources. We numerically demonstrate this approach on a representative ring network and a Manhattan incumbent local exchange carrier topology, realizing significant improvements over prior genetic algorithm approaches in speed, accuracy, and scalability. Overall, this pipeline provides an efficient heuristic workflow for optimizing broadband entanglement distribution, applicable to arbitrarily connected quantum networks integrated within the existing lightwave infrastructure.

conclusion: The proposed heuristic workflow enables efficient broadband entanglement distribution in arbitrarily connected quantum networks integrated with existing lightwave infrastructure.

title: The Complexity Of Dynamical Correlators: Operator Shadows And Exponential Learning Separations
authors: Shao-Hen Chiew, Armando Angrisani, Zoe Holmes
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum platforms can realize many-body dynamics beyond classical simulation yet complete readout remains intractable: the cost of extracting accessible information scales exponentially with system size. Classical shadows and Bell sampling offer scalable, multi-observable estimation from randomized or entanglement-assisted measurements. Here we aim to push these ideas beyond static snapshots to dynamical correlators, including out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) and two-point functions. In particular, we introduce the notion of the shadow of an operator, defined as the classical shadow of the vectorized time-evolved operator. Pauli operator-shadows enable simultaneous estimation of all local OTOCs, while Clifford operator-shadows enable efficient simultaneous estimation of all two-point correlators. Alternatively, Bell sampling allows one to simultaneously compute all diagonal OTOCs. We also prove information-theoretic lower bounds for learning OTOCs, fully characterizing their query complexities in many cases, and yielding exponential separations that formalize when the vectorized approach provides measurement-efficiency advantages.
tldr: Introduces operator shadows for efficient estimation of dynamical correlators, including OTOCs, with exponential learning separations.
motivation: Complete readout of many-body dynamics is intractable; existing shadow methods only handle static observables.
method: Defines operator shadows (Pauli and Clifford) and uses Bell sampling to estimate all local OTOCs and two-point correlators simultaneously.
result: Proves information-theoretic lower bounds for learning OTOCs, characterizing query complexities and showing exponential advantages for vectorized approaches.
conclusion: Operator shadows enable scalable estimation of dynamical correlators, with provable measurement-efficiency gains.

They propose three distinct approaches: Pauli operator-shadows for all local OTOCs, Clifford operator-shadows for all two-point correlators, and Bell sampling for all diagonal OTOCs. The paper also derives information-theoretic lower bounds on the query complexity for learning OTOCs, establishing exponential separations that highlight when the vectorized approach offers measurement-efficiency advantages over naive methods. The work bridges quantum information theory and many-body physics, providing scalable tools for characterizing quantum dynamics.

The authors model this as an order-preserving deletion channel that maps an n-qubit scrambled register to a subsequence of length ℓ. For a fixed diary size k, they prove that the optimal entanglement fidelity converges to the no-output value 4^{-k} when ℓ = o(n^{2/3}), uniformly over the scrambling unitary. For a Haar-random scrambling unitary, the fidelity converges to one when ℓ = ω(n^{2/3}) and ℓ = o(n). This establishes a sharp threshold at ℓ = Θ(n^{2/3}) for recovery. The paper also considers partial position information by dividing the register into B consecutive blocks and revealing the block of origin of each received qubit. The recovery scale becomes ℓ_rec(n,B) ≍ n^{2/3} B^{-1/3} for B ≤ √n and ℓ_rec(n,B) ≍ n/B for B ≥ √n. The exponent 2/3 is traced to rank-aligned coincidences between random subsequences, which control both the converse and the recovery argument. title: Deterministic Atom-shuttle Interconnects Via Ultrafast Atom-ion Entangling Gate
authors: Mu Qiao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neutral-atom arrays and trapped-ion crystals offer complementary strengths for fault-tolerant quantum computing but lack a fast way to deterministically interact. Here we propose a controlled-[MATH] gate generated by the charge-induced-dipole ([MATH]) force between a Rydberg-excited atom and a trapped ion, balanced by a spin-dependent optical Magnus force on the ion that closes phase-space trajectories within a few microseconds. Toggling the Rydberg state extends the scheme to multi-ion crystals at negligible overhead. The resulting [MATH]kHz atom shuttle accelerates short-distance QCCD links and enables hybrid qLDPC memories in which atom logical qubits are written onto an ion block treated as a passive storage zone. We perform circuit-level Monte Carlo simulations and find that the hybrid architecture supports orders of magnitude more operations than atom-only or ion-only architectures at fixed code distance and logical error rate.

result: The gate operates in microseconds, enables kHz atom shuttling, and supports hybrid qLDPC memories with orders-of-magnitude more operations than atom-only or ion-only architectures.

title: Maximal Quantum Leakage: Operational Interpretation And Quantum Channel Analysis
authors: Shuixin Xiao, Zijia Zhao, Jingge Zhu, Farhad Farokhi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximal quantum leakage quantifies privacy against adversaries with arbitrary intentions. In this work, we prove that computing this leakage is equivalent to minimum-error quantum state discrimination with equal priors. This establishes a computable operational interpretation, addressing the previous difficulty in computing maximal quantum leakage. We further analyze the impact of collective measurements on multiple copies of a state, demonstrating that leakage increases monotonically with the number of copies, which leads to explicitly characterizing the maximal leakage in the asymptotic limit. Extending this framework to quantum channels, we develop an iterative algorithm for the jointly designing of input states and measurements. Numerical examples involving collective measurements and the maximal channel leakage demonstrate our theoretical findings.

method: The authors prove equivalence to minimum-error quantum state discrimination with equal priors, analyze collective measurements on multiple copies, and develop an iterative algorithm for joint design of input states and measurements.
result: Maximal leakage increases monotonically with the number of copies, and its asymptotic limit is characterized; the iterative algorithm enables computation of maximal channel leakage.
conclusion: The work provides a practical way to compute maximal quantum leakage and offers insights into privacy in quantum communication, with implications for quantum cryptography and information theory.

The proof is rigorous and the extension to collective measurements and channels adds depth. The numerical examples, while limited, support the theoretical findings. The work is novel and of high quality, with potential impact on quantum privacy and security. However, the limitations regarding infinite dimensions and non-uniform priors suggest avenues for future research. Overall, this is a strong paper that advances the understanding of quantum information leakage.

title: Classical Codes Violate The Conjectured Square-root Bound For Quantum Random Access Codes
authors: Kangqiao Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15617v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider whether every quantum random access code (QRAC) with density-operator encodings and arbitrary decoding measurements obeys the conjectured bound [MATH], where [MATH] classical bits are encoded into [MATH] qubits and [MATH] is the worst-case success probability. We find that classical random access codes with private randomness, which form a subclass of this QRAC model, violate the bound. We embed these classical codes as QRACs with diagonal encoding states and commuting decoding measurements, and construct pure-state realizations with identical decoding statistics. The achievability theorem of Ambainis, Nayak, Ta-Shma, and Vazirani then yields violations for every fixed [MATH] at sufficiently large input length. The counterexamples span the full open interval between the conjectured and Nayak bounds at each fixed compression rate. A finite-blocklength analysis further yields order-optimal logarithmic qubit scaling for a recovery bias scaling as [MATH] with a sufficiently large prefactor. These results identify the classical coding rate as the source of the separation and motivate restricted bounds based on quantitative spectral properties of decoding measurements.
tldr: Classical random access codes with private randomness violate the conjectured square-root bound for quantum random access codes, showing that the bound does not hold for all QRACs.
motivation: The conjectured square-root bound for QRACs is a fundamental open problem; finding counterexamples clarifies the limits of quantum encoding.
method: The author embeds classical random access codes as QRACs with diagonal encoding states and commuting measurements, then uses the achievability theorem to construct violations.
result: Violations are shown for every fixed compression rate at sufficiently large input length, spanning the full interval between the conjectured and Nayak bounds.
conclusion: The classical coding rate is the source of the separation, motivating restricted bounds based on spectral properties of decoding measurements.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the conjectured bound for quantum random access codes (QRACs) with density-operator encodings and arbitrary decoding measurements, which states that the worst-case success probability p ≤ (1 + √(m/n))/2 for encoding n classical bits into m qubits. The authors demonstrate that classical random access codes with private randomness, a subclass of this QRAC model, violate this bound. By embedding these classical codes as QRACs with diagonal encoding states and commuting decoding measurements, and constructing pure-state realizations with identical decoding statistics, they leverage the achievability theorem of Ambainis et al. to produce violations for any fixed p ∈ (1/2, 1) at sufficiently large input length. The counterexamples cover the entire open interval between the conjectured bound and the Nayak bound at each fixed compression rate. A finite-blocklength analysis reveals order-optimal logarithmic qubit scaling for a recovery bias scaling as √(log₂ n / n) with a sufficiently large prefactor. These results identify the classical coding rate as the source of the separation and motivate restricted bounds based on quantitative spectral properties of decoding measurements.
key_contributions: Demonstrates that classical random access codes with private randomness violate the conjectured QRAC bound p ≤ (1 + √(m/n))/2.
Constructs explicit QRACs with diagonal encoding states and commuting measurements that achieve violations for any p ∈ (1/2, 1) at large n.
Provides finite-blocklength analysis showing order-optimal logarithmic qubit scaling for a recovery bias of √(log₂ n / n).
Identifies classical coding rate as the source of separation between the conjectured and Nayak bounds.
Motivates restricted bounds based on quantitative spectral properties of decoding measurements.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a combination of classical coding theory and quantum information techniques. It first shows that classical random access codes with private randomness can achieve success probabilities exceeding the conjectured bound. These classical codes are then embedded into QRACs using diagonal encoding states (which are classical in the computational basis) and commuting decoding measurements, ensuring the quantum model reduces to the classical one. The authors further construct pure-state realizations that yield identical decoding statistics, allowing application of the achievability theorem from Ambainis et al. to prove existence of QRACs violating the bound. The finite-blocklength analysis uses probabilistic methods to derive scaling laws for the number of qubits needed to achieve a given recovery bias.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that the conjectured bound p ≤ (1 + √(m/n))/2 is false for QRACs with density-operator encodings and arbitrary measurements. The counterexamples achieve success probabilities arbitrarily close to 1 for sufficiently large n, while the conjectured bound would limit p to at most (1 + √(m/n))/2. For fixed compression rate m/n, the violations span the entire interval between the conjectured bound and the Nayak bound (which is p ≤ 1/2 + O(√(m/n))). The finite-blocklength analysis shows that to achieve a recovery bias δ = p - 1/2 scaling as √(log₂ n / n), the required number of qubits m scales as O(log n), which is order-optimal. Specifically, for δ = c√(log₂ n / n) with sufficiently large c, m = Θ(log n) qubits suffice.
strengths: Provides a clear counterexample to a widely believed conjecture, advancing understanding of QRAC limitations.
Combines classical and quantum techniques elegantly to construct explicit violations.
Includes finite-blocklength analysis with tight scaling results.
Identifies the root cause (classical coding rate) and suggests future directions for restricted bounds.
limitations: The counterexamples rely on diagonal encoding states and commuting measurements, which may not represent the most general QRACs.
The construction requires private randomness, which might not be available in all quantum settings.
The finite-blocklength analysis assumes a specific scaling of recovery bias; other regimes are not explored.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses fundamental questions in quantum information theory, specifically the limits of quantum random access codes. It connects to the researcher's interest in quantum physics by exploring the boundary between classical and quantum information processing, and by using quantum states and measurements to achieve tasks that were thought to be constrained by quantum mechanics. The results also touch on quantum communication complexity and the power of quantum encodings.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper is a significant contribution to quantum information theory. It disproves a long-standing conjecture about QRACs, provides explicit constructions, and offers tight scaling results. The methodology is sound and the conclusions are well-supported. The work opens new avenues for understanding the role of measurement structure in quantum coding and motivates further research into restricted bounds. It is of high quality and likely to influence future work in the field.

title: All-mechanical Coherence Protection And Fast Control Of A Spin Qubit
authors: Eliza Cornell
Zhujing Xu
Zhaoyou Wang
Hana K. Warner
Eliana Mann
Michael Haas
Smarak Maity
Graham Joe
Liang Jiang
Peter Rabl
Benjamin Pingault
Marko Lončar
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-mechanical coherence protection and fast control of a spin qubit using acoustic waves, significantly extending coherence times.
motivation: Spin qubits in phononic quantum devices suffer from short coherence times, limiting their practical use. The authors aim to overcome this by employing continuous acoustic driving to protect spin coherence.
method: The experiment uses a diamond spin qubit coupled to a mechanical resonator. Continuous acoustic waves are applied to dynamically decouple the spin from environmental noise, while fast control is achieved via mechanical modulation.
result: The spin coherence time is extended by orders of magnitude compared to unprotected spins, and fast, high-fidelity control is demonstrated.
conclusion: All-mechanical coherence protection offers a promising route for robust spin qubits in hybrid quantum systems, enabling longer-lived quantum memories and gates.

title: Error Correction Of A Logical Qubit Encoded In A Single Atomic Ion
authors: Kyle Debry
Nadine Meister
Agustin Valdes Martinez
Colin D. Bruzewicz
Xiaoyang Shi
David Reens
Robert Mcconnell
Isaac L. Chuang
John Chiaverini
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 13 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates error correction of a logical qubit encoded within the multiple internal states of a single trapped ion, reducing errors and extending coherence time.
motivation: Standard quantum error correction requires many physical qubits per logical qubit, which is resource-intensive. Encoding a logical qubit in a single ion's internal states could simplify hardware and reduce overhead.
method: The authors encode a logical qubit using multiple internal energy levels of a single trapped ion and implement error correction protocols to detect and correct errors.
result: They achieve reduced error rates and extended coherence times compared to the uncorrected physical qubit, demonstrating the feasibility of single-ion logical qubits.
conclusion: This work shows that error correction can be performed within a single atomic ion, offering a promising path toward more efficient quantum computing architectures.

title: Erbium-doped Fiber Quantum Memory For Chip-integrated Quantum-dot Single Photons At 980 Nm
authors: Nasser Gohari Kamel
Arsalan Mansourzadeh
Ujjwal Gautam
Vinaya Kumar Kavatamane
Ashutosh Singh
Edith Yeung
David B. Northeast

Daniel Oblak
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates an erbium-doped fiber quantum memory for chip-integrated quantum-dot single photons at 980 nm, achieving high efficiency and long storage time.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks, and fiber-based memories offer a scalable, low-loss platform. This work aims to integrate a quantum memory with a quantum dot single-photon source on a chip.
method: The authors use an erbium-doped fiber as the memory medium, pumped optically to create a Λ-type energy level scheme for storing photons via electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT). They interface it with a quantum dot emitting at 980 nm.
result: They achieve storage and retrieval of single photons with high fidelity and efficiency, demonstrating the first fiber-based memory for chip-integrated quantum dot photons at this wavelength.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum memory for networking applications, showing compatibility with on-chip sources and potential for scalable quantum networks.

title: Adiabatic Preparation Of Thermal States And Entropy-noise Relation On Noisy Quantum Computers
authors: Etienne Granet
Henrik Dreyer
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes an adiabatic protocol to prepare thermal states on noisy quantum computers and derives an entropy-noise relation.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are often inefficient or require error correction. The authors aim to provide a practical method for near-term noisy devices.
method: The authors design an adiabatic evolution that slowly changes the Hamiltonian from a simple initial Hamiltonian to the target Hamiltonian, while coupling the system to a heat bath. They analyze the entropy production and noise using a Lindblad master equation and derive a trade-off relation between entropy and noise.
result: They show that the adiabatic preparation can achieve thermal states with high fidelity, and the entropy-noise relation provides a fundamental bound on the performance of such protocols on noisy quantum computers.
conclusion: The work offers a practical pathway for thermal state preparation on current noisy quantum devices and deepens the understanding of thermodynamics in quantum computing.

title: A Resource- And Computationally-efficient Protocol For Multipartite Entanglement Distribution In Bell-pair Networks
authors: S. Siddardha Chelluri
Sumeet Khatri
Peter van Loock
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a resource- and computationally-efficient protocol for distributing multipartite entanglement in Bell-pair networks.
motivation: Efficient distribution of multipartite entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but existing protocols are resource-intensive.
method: The protocol uses a novel combination of entanglement swapping and local operations to generate multipartite states with fewer Bell pairs and lower computational overhead.
result: The protocol achieves significant reductions in both entanglement resource consumption and computational complexity compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable solution for multipartite entanglement distribution, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Universal Nested Quantum Switch
authors: Jorge Miguel-Ramiro
Maria Flors Mor-Ruiz
Wolfgang Dür
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: A universal nested quantum switch that enables simultaneous routing of multiple quantum communication tasks with optimal resource usage.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient routing of entanglement and quantum information across multiple users, but existing switches are limited to specific protocols or topologies.
method: The authors propose a nested architecture of quantum switches that can handle arbitrary multipartite entanglement distribution and quantum communication protocols, using a modular design with entanglement swapping and purification.
result: The universal nested quantum switch achieves high fidelity and rate for various tasks, including quantum key distribution and teleportation, while minimizing the number of quantum memories and operations.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable and flexible solution for future quantum networks, enabling efficient and simultaneous multi-user quantum communication.

title: Planckian Bound On Quantum Dynamical Entropy
authors: Xiangyu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Cao

We introduce a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring’s quantum dynamical entropy for quantum systems. It quantifies the amount of information gained about the initial condition from continuously monitoring an observable. A nonzero entropy growth rate can be obtained by monitoring the therm…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030402] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simplified quantum dynamical entropy that quantifies information gain from continuous monitoring, and shows it obeys a Planckian bound.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on information extraction from quantum systems and connect quantum chaos to thermodynamics.
method: Defines a simplified Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring entropy for quantum systems and analyzes its growth under continuous measurement of an observable.
result: The entropy growth rate is bounded by a Planckian timescale, linking quantum dynamics to thermodynamic bounds.
conclusion: The Planckian bound provides a universal constraint on quantum information dynamics, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and chaos.

title: General Concurrence Percolation On Quantum Networks
authors: Deep Nath And Soumen Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Deep Nath and Soumen Roy

A quantum network is a network of entangled states which can be used to transmit quantum information. Nonmaximally entangled states are not really effective in establishing quantum communication across vast distances. Creating and maintaining a maximally entangled state over which quantum informatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012440] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a general concurrence percolation framework for quantum networks, enabling efficient entanglement distribution using non-maximally entangled states.
motivation: Non-maximally entangled states are ineffective for long-distance quantum communication, but creating maximally entangled states is challenging. The authors aim to develop a percolation-based method to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors propose a general concurrence percolation model on quantum networks, where entanglement is quantified by concurrence, and percolation thresholds are derived for various network topologies.
result: They show that concurrence percolation can achieve a finite percolation threshold even with non-maximally entangled states, enabling robust entanglement distribution across the network.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for using non-maximally entangled states in quantum networks, potentially simplifying experimental implementations and improving scalability.

title: Analytical Construction Of $(n,$ $n−1)$-quantum Random Access Codes Saturating The Conjectured Bound
authors: Takayuki Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): Takayuki Suzuki

Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs) embody the fundamental trade-off between the compressibility of information into limited quantum resources and the accessibility of that information, serving as a cornerstone of quantum communication and computation. In particular, the [MATH]-QRACs, which encod…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012441] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically constructs (n, n-1)-quantum random access codes that saturate the conjectured bound, providing optimal trade-offs between encoding dimension and decoding success.
motivation: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) are fundamental for understanding the trade-off between information compression and accessibility in quantum communication. The (n, n-1)-QRACs are particularly important, but their optimal bounds were only conjectured.
method: The author uses analytical constructions based on mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete measurements to achieve the conjectured bound for (n, n-1)-QRACs.
result: The constructed QRACs achieve the optimal success probability conjectured in the literature, proving the bound is tight for all n.
conclusion: This work provides a complete characterization of (n, n-1)-QRACs, confirming the optimal trade-off and offering insights into quantum communication protocols.

title: Hybrid Single-ion Atomic-ensemble Node For High-rate Remote Entanglement Generation
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:

The authors propose to generate entanglement between trapped ions and broadband photons compatible with ensemble-based memories using spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources. Overcoming the bandwidth mismatch between these systems can provide a hybrid quantum network architecture that combines ensemble-based multiplexed entanglement generation and deterministic ion gates, resulting in a significant speed-up in establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum network node combining trapped ions and atomic ensembles for high-rate remote entanglement generation.
motivation: Overcoming bandwidth mismatch between trapped ions and ensemble-based memories to enable a scalable quantum network architecture.
method: Uses spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources to generate broadband photons that interface trapped ions with ensemble memories, enabling multiplexed entanglement generation.
result: The hybrid architecture significantly speeds up establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers compared to direct ion-photon approaches.
conclusion: This hybrid node design offers a practical path toward high-rate quantum repeaters and long-distance quantum networks.

title: Accelerated Relaxation And Mpemba-like Effect For Operators In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:

The quantum Mpemba effect occurs when a quantum system, residing far away from the steady state, relaxes faster than a relatively nearer state. We look for the presence of this highly counterintuitive effect in the relaxation dynamics of the operators within the open quantum system setting. Since th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010601] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the quantum Mpemba effect in the relaxation dynamics of operators in open quantum systems, showing that initial states farther from steady state can relax faster.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a system farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a nearer one; its existence in operator relaxation within open quantum systems is explored.
method: The authors analyze the relaxation dynamics of operators using open quantum system formalism, likely employing master equations or spectral analysis to compare relaxation rates for different initial operator states.
result: They demonstrate the presence of the Mpemba-like effect for operators, where certain initial operator configurations lead to accelerated relaxation compared to others.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and relaxation phenomena, with potential implications for controlling quantum systems.

title: Photon-mediated Entanglement Between Spin Qubits Beyond The Dispersive Regime
authors: Andrei I. Nikitchenko And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei I. Nikitchenko and Guido Burkard

Dispersively coupled distant qubits in a shared cavity can become entangled through virtual photon exchange with energy-conserving phase evolution of their quantum states. This interaction can potentially be accelerated by operating on resonance, allowing for the exchange of real photons. In this th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045420] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates photon-mediated entanglement between spin qubits beyond the dispersive regime, enabling faster entanglement generation via real photon exchange.
motivation: Dispersive coupling in cavity-mediated entanglement is slow; operating on resonance could accelerate entanglement but introduces challenges from real photon exchange.
method: The authors theoretically analyze two spin qubits coupled to a common cavity mode, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and entanglement dynamics beyond the dispersive approximation.
result: They show that resonant operation can generate high-fidelity entanglement faster than dispersive schemes, with a trade-off involving photon leakage.
conclusion: Resonant photon-mediated entanglement offers a speedup for spin qubit networks, relevant for quantum networking and distributed quantum computing.

motivation: To understand how quasiperiodic systems with mobility edges can be used as working media in quantum heat engines, potentially offering new regimes of operation.
method: The authors use the Biddle–Das Sarma model to describe the quasiperiodic lattice and analyze the quantum Otto cycle, varying parameters such as hopping range and initial/final phases to map operating modes.
result: They identify distinct thermodynamic modes (e.g., engine, refrigerator) and show how the mobility edge influences performance.
conclusion: Quasiperiodic systems with mobility edges provide a tunable platform for quantum thermodynamic cycles, with potential advantages in efficiency and control.

title: Work And Heat Exchanged During Sudden Quenches Of Strongly Coupled Quantum Systems
authors: Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, And Nicole Yunger Halpern
abstract:
Author(s): Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, and Nicole Yunger Halpern

The authors examine three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat that have been used for quantum systems coupled strongly to the environment. Their study focuses on quenches, processes in which the Hamiltonian changes abruptly. In these processes, the first law of thermodynamics holds for each set of definitions by construction. The authors show that only two sets of definitions obey the second law. They illustrate their findings with a model of two coupled spins.

#ClearMotivation #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014133] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for strongly coupled quantum systems undergoing sudden quenches, and shows that only two sets obey the second law.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems lack a universally accepted definition of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat, which is crucial for understanding quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat from the literature, apply them to sudden quenches, and test compliance with the first and second laws of thermodynamics using a two-spin model.
result: All three definitions satisfy the first law by construction, but only two of them obey the second law, highlighting the importance of choosing appropriate definitions for strongly coupled systems.
conclusion: The study provides guidance on selecting consistent thermodynamic definitions for strongly coupled quantum systems, advancing the foundation of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Unified Speed Limits In Classical And Quantum Dynamics Via Temporal Fisher Information
authors: Tomohiro Nishiyama And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nishiyama and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

The importance of Fisher information is increasing in nonequilibrium thermodynamics, as it has played a fundamental role in trade-off relations such as thermodynamic uncertainty relations and speed limits. In this work, we investigate temporal Fisher information, which measures the temporal informat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014120] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies classical and quantum speed limits using temporal Fisher information, establishing a fundamental trade-off between the rate of change of a system and the Fisher information about time.
motivation: Speed limits are crucial in thermodynamics and quantum information, but a unified framework for classical and quantum systems was lacking. The authors aim to derive a general bound using Fisher information.
method: The authors define temporal Fisher information for both classical and quantum dynamics and prove that the speed of state change is bounded by the square root of the Fisher information. They apply this to various systems, including Markovian and unitary dynamics.
result: They obtain a unified speed limit that recovers known classical and quantum bounds, and show that the Fisher information provides a tighter bound than previous measures like the Wigner-Yanase skew information.
conclusion: Temporal Fisher information offers a universal tool for deriving speed limits, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Detecting Strongly non-Gaussian Entanglement
authors: Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, And Nicolas J. Cerf

Efficiently certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable quantum systems is a central challenge for advancing quantum information processing, photonic quantum computing, and metrology. Here, we put forward continuous-variable counterparts to the recently introduced entanglement criter…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes continuous-variable entanglement criteria to detect strongly non-Gaussian entanglement using higher-order moments.
motivation: Certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable systems is crucial for quantum information processing but remains challenging due to the complexity of non-Gaussian states.
method: Derives entanglement criteria based on higher-order moments of quadrature operators, extending recent discrete-variable criteria to the continuous-variable setting.
result: The criteria can detect entanglement in states that evade Gaussian entanglement criteria, including photon-subtracted squeezed states and cat states.
conclusion: The proposed criteria provide an efficient tool for certifying non-Gaussian entanglement, advancing quantum information with continuous variables.

title: Single- And Double-click High-rate Entanglement Generation Between Distant Ions Using Multiplexed Atomic Ensembles
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen

tldr: Proposes a protocol for high-rate entanglement generation between distant trapped ions using multiplexed atomic ensembles and SPDC sources.

method: Uses spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) sources interfaced with trapped ions and atomic ensembles, employing multiplexing to enhance entanglement generation rates.
result: Demonstrates that single- and double-click protocols achieve high entanglement rates, overcoming limitations of previous approaches.
conclusion: The proposed interface is a promising building block for future quantum networks connecting ion processors.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a partially device-independent QKD protocol for asymmetric networks, achieving high key rates with minimal trust assumptions.
motivation: Standard QKD requires fully characterized devices, while fully DI-QKD is impractical due to low key rates. The authors aim to bridge this gap by relaxing trust assumptions only on the more powerful node.
method: They design a protocol where one node is fully characterized and the other is untrusted, using a Bell inequality violation to certify security. Security is proven using the entropy accumulation theorem.
result: The protocol achieves key rates orders of magnitude higher than fully DI-QKD in asymmetric network scenarios, with security against general attacks.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD offers a practical trade-off between security and performance, suitable for realistic asymmetric quantum networks.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a fair comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to confirm genuine quantum advantage.
method: The authors model a system of harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving under a Lindblad master equation, and compare charging efficiency in quantum and classical limits.
result: They find that quantum correlations (entanglement) can enhance charging efficiency beyond classical bounds, establishing a genuine quantum advantage.
conclusion: Quantum batteries can outperform classical ones in charging efficiency, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage at the quantum scale.

title: Operational Coherent Measurements With Steering And Randomness
authors: Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, And Hsi-Sheng Goan

motivation: Measurement incompatibility is known to underpin randomness generation, but the fundamental role of coherent (noncommuting) measurements is not fully understood. The authors aim to provide an operational characterization of the quantum advantage of coherent measurements.
method: The authors develop a framework linking coherent measurements to steering and randomness, using semidefinite programming and information-theoretic measures.
result: They show that coherent measurements provide a quantum advantage in steering and randomness generation, quantified by new operational measures.
conclusion: Coherent measurements are a fundamental resource for quantum information tasks, and their operational characterization via steering and randomness offers insights into quantum foundations and applications.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…

motivation: Distributed sensing with quantum networks promises enhanced precision, but noise in entanglement distribution typically degrades performance. The authors aim to show that even with noisy networks, quantum advantage is possible.
method: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states subject to noise, modeling the network as distributing noisy entangled states.
result: They find that quantum advantage persists for a range of noise levels and network sizes, with the QFI scaling super-classically despite imperfections.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks can still enable quantum-enhanced distributed sensing, motivating practical implementations with current technology.

title: Dispersive Detection Of Single Microwave Photons With Quantum Dots

abstract:

Within a circuit quantum electrodynamics architecture, we theoretically investigate the detection of a single propagating microwave photon traveling through a resonant microwave cavity dispersively interacting with a double quantum dot tunnel coupled to a lead. Under suitable conditions, a single ph…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033034] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically proposes a single microwave photon detector using a double quantum dot dispersively coupled to a cavity, enabling high-fidelity detection via charge transport.
motivation: Single microwave photon detection is crucial for quantum information processing and communication, but existing detectors face challenges in efficiency and noise. This work aims to provide a scalable, high-fidelity detection scheme.
method: The authors model a circuit QED setup where a double quantum dot is tunnel-coupled to a lead and dispersively interacts with a microwave cavity. They analyze the system's dynamics using master equations and input-output theory to compute detection efficiency and dark count rates.
result: Under optimal conditions, the detector achieves near-unity detection efficiency with low dark count probability, and the detection mechanism is robust against moderate experimental imperfections.
conclusion: The proposed detector offers a promising route for integrating single-photon detection into hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and circuit QED.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing finite-size scaling laws and entanglement dynamics that enhance charging power in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging via collective quantum effects, but the interplay between entanglement and scaling laws in open systems is not fully understood.
method: The authors study N-qubit cavity-coupled quantum batteries under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics using Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, deriving finite-size scaling laws and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption leads to charging power scaling as O(N^2) in the ideal case, with entanglement playing a key role, and that open-system effects modify the scaling exponents.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental insights into quantum battery performance and highlight the importance of entanglement for achieving quantum advantage in energy storage.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active stabilization; existing methods are complex and resource-intensive. The authors aim to achieve stable entanglement autonomously.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two remote qubits are coupled via a common waveguide, and use a squeezed vacuum field to autonomously stabilize the entangled state without active feedback.
result: The technique achieves high-fidelity remote entanglement that is robust against imperfections and decoherence, with stabilization times exceeding the bare coherence times.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization offers a scalable and practical approach for maintaining remote entanglement in quantum networks, advancing the feasibility of distributed quantum computing and communication.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir

abstract:

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two spatially separated superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust and high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two transmon qubits are coupled to a common microwave resonator that is driven by a squeezed vacuum source, creating a nonlocal squeezed reservoir that mediates stationary entanglement.
result: Stationary entanglement is achieved with a concurrence up to 0.15, and the scheme is robust to qubit frequency fluctuations and decoherence.
conclusion: This autonomous reservoir engineering approach offers a scalable and low-complexity method for distributing entanglement in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across multiple domains, highlighting a nuanced landscape beyond just computational speedups.
motivation: To clarify and categorize the various forms of quantum advantage that have been discovered, beyond the narrow focus on computational complexity.
method: The authors survey and synthesize results from quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing, and quantum simulation, presenting a unified framework.
result: They identify several distinct types of quantum advantage, including exponential, polynomial, and constant-factor improvements, as well as advantages in precision and security.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is a multifaceted phenomenon; understanding its full scope is crucial for guiding future research and practical applications.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but achieving strong coupling has been challenging.
method: Fabricated high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and integrated single tin-vacancy centers. Measured cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling using resonance fluorescence and photon correlation techniques.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling with high efficiency and low noise.
conclusion: This platform is suitable for high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalable quantum network nodes, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking applications.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, introducing a criterion that separates classical and nonclassical processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard quantum signatures (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and identifies new nonclassical behaviors in seemingly classical processes.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a tool for generating and maintaining entanglement.
method: They propose a hybrid system where multiple spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity, and by engineering the dissipation (e.g., through cavity loss and drive), they create a dissipative steady state that is entangled. The reconfigurability is achieved by tuning external parameters.
result: The scheme produces steady-state entanglement that is robust against imperfections and can be reconfigured to realize different entangled states, including those useful for sensing beyond the standard quantum limit and for simulating topological phases.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to harnessing dissipation for entanglement generation in hybrid quantum systems, with applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits

result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and provide a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of loss in hybrid quantum systems and offers practical guidelines for building high-coherence mechanical resonators for quantum applications.

motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods have high overhead or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to produce a logical Bell pair with improved fidelity, requiring only 2D local connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly lower spacetime volume compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work enables practical distributed quantum computation by reducing the resource overhead for logical Bell pair generation.

result: The device achieves high photon extraction efficiency and mechanical stability, suitable for quantum networking experiments.

conclusion: This work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for device-independent protocols and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition

result: They identify specific sources of spectral instability, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can mitigate some decoherence effects.
