[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014129] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions as a model of biased anomalous transport.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion is common in complex media, and biased transport (e.g., due to external fields) is important in many systems. The authors aim to develop a CTRW model that captures both asymmetric waiting times and jump lengths.
method: The authors formulate a CTRW with coupled asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions, and derive the mean-squared displacement and other transport properties analytically and via simulations.
result: The model produces a variety of anomalous diffusion regimes, including subdiffusion, superdiffusion, and biased transport, depending on the parameters of the distributions.
conclusion: The proposed CTRW model provides a flexible framework for describing biased anomalous transport in heterogeneous media.

title: Universality Of Order Statistics For Brownian Reshuffling
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, And Tomasz Maciocha
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, and Tomasz Maciocha

In a one-dimensional gas of particles confined by an asymptotically power-law potential, the ordering of the particles changes as they perform Brownian motion. The authors show that the order statistics that describe how the particles are reshuffled are universal and independent of the potential’s exponent, while the timescale of the reshuffling does depend on it.

#UniversalBehavior #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014130] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies universal order statistics in a one-dimensional gas of Brownian particles confined by a power-law potential.
motivation: Understanding how particle ordering changes over time in a diffusive system is a fundamental statistical mechanics problem.
method: The authors analytically derive the order statistics for Brownian particles in an asymptotically power-law potential, showing universality independent of the exponent.
result: The order statistics are universal, while the reshuffling timescale depends on the potential exponent.
conclusion: The work provides a universal characterization of particle reshuffling in a class of confined Brownian systems.

title: Dynamic Effects Of Electric Fields In A Hybrid-coupled Thermosensitive Neuronal Network
authors: Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, And Fernando F. Ferreira
abstract:
Author(s): Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, and Fernando F. Ferreira

The dynamics of thermosensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal networks under hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields is investigated in a ring topology. Numerical simulations show collective behavior ranging from incoherent activity to coherent traveling waves and chimera and multichimera s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014218] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of thermosensitive neuronal networks under electric fields, focusing on collective behaviors like chimera states.
motivation: Understanding how electric fields affect neuronal network dynamics is important for neuroscience, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons with hybrid synaptic coupling in a ring topology under external electric fields.
result: The network exhibits transitions from incoherent activity to traveling waves and chimera states depending on coupling and field parameters.
conclusion: Electric fields can induce complex spatiotemporal patterns in thermosensitive neuronal networks, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Distance Function For Stochastic Matrices
authors: Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, And Iain B. Styles
abstract:
Author(s): Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, and Iain B. Styles

The ability to quantify the similarity of stochastic processes is important in a wide range of areas including communications, simulation, and operational research. Such processes are commonly modeled as Markov Chains and so a natural way to compare their similarity is to compute distances between p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014125] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a distance function for stochastic matrices based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate of Markov chains.
motivation: Quantifying similarity between stochastic processes is important in communications, simulation, and operational research, but existing distance measures for Markov chains have limitations.
method: The authors define a distance function using the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov chains and prove it satisfies metric properties.
result: The proposed distance is a true metric and can be computed efficiently for finite-state Markov chains.
conclusion: The distance function provides a principled way to compare stochastic processes modeled as Markov chains.

title: Intermediate Scattering Function Of Brownian Particles In A Tilted Cosine Potential
authors: Regina Rusch And Thomas Franosch
abstract:
Author(s): Regina Rusch and Thomas Franosch

We solve the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derive the intermediate scattering function (ISF), which captures the full spatiotemporal dynamics of the system. The model consists of a single overdamped Brownian particle in one dimension. We derive a gen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014127] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derives the intermediate scattering function.
motivation: Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of Brownian particles in periodic potentials is important for condensed matter physics and soft matter.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation analytically using continued fractions and matrix methods to compute the intermediate scattering function.
result: They obtain exact expressions for the intermediate scattering function and analyze its dependence on tilt and potential strength.
conclusion: The work provides a complete analytical solution for the dynamics of a Brownian particle in a tilted periodic potential, which can be used to interpret scattering experiments.

title: Floquet Resonances In The Double Kicked Top
authors: Avadhut V. Purohit And Udaysinh T. Bhosale
abstract:
Author(s): Avadhut V. Purohit and Udaysinh T. Bhosale

We study exact quantum resonances in the double kicked top (DKT), a driven spin model that extends the quantum kicked top (QKT) by introducing an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick. By expressing the dynamics in terms of effective parameters [MATH], we analytically show the…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014214] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exact quantum resonances in a driven spin model called the double kicked top, extending the quantum kicked top with an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick.
motivation: To understand quantum resonance phenomena in periodically driven systems, which are important for quantum chaos and control.
method: Analytical derivation of effective parameters and exact resonance conditions for the double kicked top model.
result: Exact quantum resonances are identified and characterized analytically, showing how the additional kick modifies the resonance structure.
conclusion: The double kicked top exhibits rich resonance behavior that can be tuned by the second kick, providing insights into driven quantum systems.

title: Emergence Of Higher-order Interactions In Systems Of Coupled Kuramoto Oscillators With Time Delay
authors: Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, And Hiroya Nakao
abstract:
Author(s): Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, and Hiroya Nakao

We show that higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators. By expanding the delayed pairwise coupling to the second order, we derive a delay-free Kuramoto model possessing both pairwise and three-body interactions. Numerical simulations and s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014215] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that higher-order interactions emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators.
motivation: To understand how higher-order interactions can arise in systems of coupled oscillators with time delay.
method: Expanding the delayed pairwise coupling to second order to derive a delay-free Kuramoto model with pairwise and three-body interactions, then performing numerical simulations and stability analysis.
result: Higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling, and the derived model captures the dynamics.
conclusion: Time delay in pairwise coupling can effectively generate higher-order interactions, which may be relevant for complex systems.

title: Random Walks On Disordered Lattices: The Role Of Effective Porosity, Blocked Domain Width, And Spatial Correlations
authors: Nathann Teixeira Rodrigues And Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis
abstract:
Author(s): Nathann Teixeira Rodrigues and Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis

We perform a numerical study of random walks (RWs) on 3D lattices with random and periodic distributions of blocked sites, analyze the dependence of effective diffusion coefficients [MATH] on the effective porosity [MATH], and show applications to diffusive solute transport in some porous materials.…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014122] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies random walks on disordered lattices to model solute transport in porous media, focusing on effective diffusion coefficients.
motivation: Understanding diffusion in porous materials is important for applications like contaminant transport and oil recovery, but the role of disorder and spatial correlations is not fully understood.
method: Numerical simulations of random walks on 3D lattices with random and periodic blocked sites, measuring effective diffusion coefficients as a function of porosity and blocked domain width.
result: Effective diffusion coefficients depend on effective porosity and blocked domain width, with spatial correlations affecting the scaling behavior.
conclusion: The study provides insights into diffusive transport in porous media, but the work is purely classical and does not involve quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Different Phases And Phase Transition Points In Hidden Markov Models
authors: Ruben Poghosyan, Vardan Bardakhchyan, And David B. Saakian

We are looking for different phases in hidden Markov models (HMMs). By analyzing the stationary solution of the master equation, we discover different situations with localized or delocalized distributions for the stationary distributions of the master equation. We hypothesize that these phases are …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014123] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phases and phase transitions in hidden Markov models using master equation analysis.
motivation: To understand different phases (localized vs delocalized) in hidden Markov models and identify phase transition points.
method: Analyzes stationary solutions of the master equation for hidden Markov models.
result: Discovers different phases with localized or delocalized stationary distributions and hypothesizes phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the phase structure of hidden Markov models.

title: Alternating Pattern Formation In Oscillatory Media With Spatially Uniform And Nonuniform Global Feedback
authors: Zhilin Qu, Chunli Huang, And Fengze Sui
abstract:
Author(s): Zhilin Qu, Chunli Huang, and Fengze Sui

Alternating (temporally period-2) stripes, clusters, and labyrinths have been observed in chemical and biochemical reactions, in Min-protein dynamics in E. coli and in vitro systems, and in calcium alternans in cardiac myocytes. However, the mechanisms underlying the formation of these spatiotempora…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014211] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies alternating pattern formation in oscillatory media with global feedback, applied to chemical and biological systems.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms behind alternating stripes, clusters, and labyrinths observed in chemical reactions and biological systems like Min-protein dynamics and cardiac alternans.
method: The authors analyze oscillatory media with spatially uniform and nonuniform global feedback using theoretical models and simulations.
result: They identify conditions and mechanisms leading to alternating pattern formation, including period-2 temporal behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into spatiotemporal pattern formation in oscillatory systems, relevant to nonlinear dynamics and biological rhythms.

title: Filtered Rayleigh-Ritz And The Prony-Ritz Equivalence Class
authors: Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, And Michael L. Wagman
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, and Michael L. Wagman

Recent work [ 112, 054506 (2025);
tldr: This paper presents a method for extracting energy spectra from correlation functions in lattice quantum field theory using a filtered Rayleigh-Ritz approach and establishes an equivalence class with Prony-type methods.
motivation: Extracting excited-state energies and matrix elements from correlation functions is a fundamental challenge in lattice QCD, and existing methods like the Prony method and Lanczos algorithm have limitations in stability and applicability.
method: The authors introduce a filtered Rayleigh-Ritz method that uses a filter function to isolate low-energy states, and they prove its equivalence to a class of Prony-type methods, providing a unified framework.
result: The method yields stable and accurate extraction of multiple energy levels from correlation function data, with rigorous error bounds and demonstrated performance on synthetic and lattice QCD data.
conclusion: The filtered Rayleigh-Ritz method offers a robust and theoretically grounded approach for spectral extraction in lattice field theory, with connections to existing techniques that enhance understanding and applicability.

title: Intrinsic Density Of States And The Origin Of Gamma Volume Distributions In Jammed Granular Matter
authors: Ching Chang, Yang Chang, And Jason Chao
abstract:
Author(s): Ching Chang, Yang Chang, and Jason Chao

Athermal systems such as granular materials exhibit reproducible volume fluctuations despite the absence of thermal equilibration, yet a quantitative statistical-mechanical description remains incomplete. Within the Edwards ensemble, volume replaces energy as the conserved quantity and compactivity …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015410] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies volume fluctuations in jammed granular matter using the Edwards ensemble, a statistical mechanics approach for athermal systems.
motivation: Athermal granular materials exhibit reproducible volume fluctuations, but a quantitative statistical-mechanical description is lacking.
method: The authors apply the Edwards ensemble, where volume replaces energy as the conserved quantity, and compute the intrinsic density of states.
result: They derive gamma volume distributions and explain their origin from the density of states.
conclusion: The Edwards ensemble provides a valid statistical framework for understanding volume fluctuations in jammed granular matter.

title: Statistical Mechanics Of Indistinguishable Energy States And The Glass Transition
authors: Shimul Akhanjee
abstract:
Author(s): Shimul Akhanjee

The statistical mechanics of particles that populate indistinguishable energy substates is explored. In particular, the mathematical treatment of microstates differs from conventional statistical mechanics, where, for a given degeneracy, the energy sublevels or substates are universally treated as d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014119] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a modified statistical mechanics for indistinguishable energy substates to model the glass transition.
motivation: Standard statistical mechanics treats energy sublevels as distinguishable, which may not capture the physics of glassy systems where substates are indistinguishable.
method: The author develops a mathematical framework where microstates are counted differently due to indistinguishability of energy substates, leading to a new partition function.
result: The new formalism yields a thermodynamic description that exhibits a glass transition-like behavior.
conclusion: Indistinguishability of energy substates can fundamentally alter statistical mechanical predictions and may explain the glass transition.

title: Twisted State Stability Under Local Order Parameter Adaptation
authors: Xueqin Wang, Hong He, Wende Tang, Yiju Peng, And Ya Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Xueqin Wang, Hong He, Wende Tang, Yiju Peng, and Ya Jia

Twisted states commonly arise in nonlocally coupled ring networks. We study the stability of twisted states in networks with higher-order interactions under the adaptive mechanism based on the local order parameter. The adaptive feedback dynamically regulates the coupling strength and thus reshapes …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014209] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of twisted states in nonlocally coupled ring networks with higher-order interactions and adaptive coupling based on local order parameters.
motivation: Twisted states are common in coupled oscillator networks, and understanding their stability under adaptive mechanisms is important for controlling synchronization patterns.
method: The authors analyze a ring network of phase oscillators with higher-order (simplicial) interactions and introduce an adaptive feedback that adjusts coupling strengths based on the local order parameter. They perform linear stability analysis and numerical simulations.
result: They derive stability conditions for twisted states and show that the adaptive mechanism can either stabilize or destabilize certain twisted states depending on parameters.
conclusion: The adaptive coupling based on local order parameter provides a way to control the stability of twisted states in networks with higher-order interactions.

title: Energy-dynamics Interplay In Temporal Networks Triggers Explosive Synchronization
authors: Romuald Mbonwouo, Steve J. Kongni, Sishu Shankar Muni, Carmel T. Lambu, Venceslas Nguefoue, Patrick Louodop, And Thierry Njougouo
abstract:

Synchronization in networks of coupled oscillators is a fundamental problem in the study of collective behavior. In this paper we investigate the synchronization transition in networks of coupled dynamical systems from an energetic perspective. Interactions between systems/oscillators are assumed to…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014210] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies explosive synchronization in temporal networks from an energetic perspective, focusing on coupled oscillators.
motivation: Understanding synchronization transitions in networks of coupled oscillators is a fundamental problem in collective behavior.
method: The authors model interactions between oscillators with an energy-based coupling and analyze the synchronization transition using numerical simulations.
result: They find that the interplay between energy dynamics and temporal network structure triggers explosive synchronization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into synchronization phenomena but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Nanorotator In The Hypomagnetic Field: Implications For Magnetobiology

A mechanism for the biological effects of the hypomagnetic field is proposed, based on the rotational motion of a molecule as a whole within a cavity in an enzyme. It has been shown previously that a molecular rotator about 1 nm in size can have a decoherence time of up to tens of milliseconds. On s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014406] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum nanorotator mechanism for biological effects of hypomagnetic fields.
motivation: To explain how weak magnetic fields can affect biological systems, which is not well understood.
method: Models a molecular rotator in an enzyme cavity with quantum decoherence and rotational dynamics.
result: Shows that the rotator can have long decoherence times and respond to hypomagnetic fields.
conclusion: The mechanism may account for magnetobiological effects, but remains speculative.

title: Hamiltonian Active Particles In Incompressible Fluid Membranes
authors: Sneha Krishnan And Rickmoy Samanta

Active proteins and membrane-bound motors exert force dipole flows along fluid interfaces and lipid bilayers. We develop a Hamiltonian framework for the interactions of pusher and puller dipoles embedded in an incompressible two-dimensional membrane supported by a shallow viscous subphase. Beginning…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015102] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a Hamiltonian framework for active particles exerting force dipoles in incompressible fluid membranes.
motivation: To understand interactions of active proteins and membrane-bound motors in biological membranes.
method: The authors construct a Hamiltonian model for pusher and puller dipoles embedded in a 2D incompressible membrane supported by a shallow viscous subphase.
result: The framework captures the dynamics of active particles in fluid membranes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for studying active matter in biological membranes.

title: Polarization Conversion In Time-modulated Magnetized Plasmas: Faraday Configuration
authors: Hossein Mehrpour Bernety, Dikshitulu K. Kalluri, And Mark A. Cappelli

In this paper, we address the problem of wave propagation within an unbounded time-modulated magnetized plasma in a Faraday configuration. We present an analysis formulated by coupling Maxwell's equations with the hydrodynamic evolution equation for the plasma current density, and casting the result…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015210] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave propagation and polarization conversion in time-modulated magnetized plasmas, which is a classical electrodynamics problem with no quantum information or thermodynamics content.
motivation: To understand how time modulation of plasma parameters affects wave polarization in a Faraday configuration, which may have applications in classical wave manipulation.
method: The authors couple Maxwell's equations with the hydrodynamic plasma current density equation and solve the resulting system analytically or numerically for the Faraday configuration.
result: The paper presents an analysis of polarization conversion effects due to time modulation of the magnetized plasma.
conclusion: Time modulation can be used to control polarization in plasmas, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Autoparametric Excitation Of An Elastic Chain In A Periodic Potential
authors: Johann Maddi, Christophe Coste, And Michel Saint Jean
abstract:

We describe the motions of an elastic chain submitted to an external periodic potential, without dissipation. Initially, the energy is injected in a single eigenmode of the chain. We show that this eigenmode acts as a parametric forcing of the other modes, and since there is no external energy sourc…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015504] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the autoparametric excitation of an elastic chain in a periodic potential without dissipation, focusing on energy transfer between eigenmodes.
motivation: To understand how energy injected into a single eigenmode of an elastic chain can parametrically excite other modes in the absence of external energy sources.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the dynamics of an elastic chain under a periodic potential, modeling the energy injection into one eigenmode and studying the parametric forcing of other modes.
result: They show that the initially excited eigenmode acts as a parametric pump for other modes, leading to energy redistribution among modes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear mode coupling in elastic systems, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Combinatorial Reasoning For Large Language Models
authors: Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, And Narendra N. Hegade

We design and implement a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models (QCR-LLM), integrating a real quantum computer in the hybrid workflow. QCR-LLM reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem. In this sense, reasoning fragme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033070] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models, integrating a real quantum computer to reformulate reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem.
motivation: Large language models often struggle with complex reasoning tasks; the authors aim to leverage quantum computing to enhance reasoning aggregation.
method: The framework reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) problem and solves it using a quantum computer in a hybrid classical-quantum workflow.
result: The approach demonstrates improved reasoning accuracy on selected benchmarks compared to classical baselines.
conclusion: Quantum combinatorial optimization can be effectively integrated with large language models to improve reasoning capabilities.

title: Programmable Transport Of Rotating Particles In Obstacle Arrays

Rotating colloids, or spinners, in obstacle arrays exhibit frequency-set stationary orbits and currents set by the competition between an inertial, Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033071] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transport of rotating colloids in obstacle arrays using simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic lift and particle currents.
motivation: Understanding the motion of rotating particles in complex environments is important for microfluidics and particle separation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations are used to model rotating colloids in obstacle arrays, capturing hydrodynamic coupling and lift forces.
result: The simulations reveal frequency-set stationary orbits and currents determined by the competition between Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the transport of spinners in obstacle arrays, but it is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Detection Time Distribution Predicted Using Absorbing Boundary Conditions And Imaginary Potentials
authors: Alireza Jozani And Roderich Tumulka

There are several inequivalent proposals in the literature for how to compute the probability distribution of the time that a detector registers for the arrival of a quantum particle. For three of these proposals, based on two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials, we compu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033072] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares three proposals for computing detection time distributions in quantum mechanics using absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
motivation: There are multiple inequivalent proposals for the probability distribution of detection times, and the authors aim to compare their predictions.
method: The authors compute the detection time distribution for three proposals: two based on absorbing boundary conditions and one using imaginary potentials.
result: The three proposals yield different predictions for the detection time distribution.
conclusion: The choice of boundary condition or potential significantly affects the predicted detection time distribution, highlighting the need for experimental discrimination.

title: Shell Formation And Two-dimensional Nanofriction In Three-dimensional Ion Coulomb Crystals
authors: L. A. Rüffert And T. E. Mehlstäubler

Building on prior work that used 2D ion crystals to investigate one-dimensional nanofr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033044] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shell formation and nanofriction in 3D ion Coulomb crystals, which is a topic in classical/quantum many-body physics and tribology, not directly related to the user's research interests.
motivation: Understanding nanofriction at curved interfaces using self-organized ion crystals as a model system.
method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of concentric shell structures in 3D ion Coulomb crystals in a linear Paul trap, studying their mechanical properties and friction.
result: Observation of shell formation and measurement of nanofriction forces between shells.
conclusion: Ion Coulomb crystals provide a platform for studying two-dimensional nanofriction on curved surfaces.

title: Kramers Dichroism In $PT$-symmetric Magnets
authors: Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, And Justin C. W. Song

The quantum states in doubly degenerate Kramers pairs can act as an internal degree of freedom. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033046] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets, a condensed matter phenomenon with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how circularly polarized light can selectively polarize Kramers pairs in PT-symmetric magnets, enabling control of internal degrees of freedom.
method: The authors theoretically analyze interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light in PT-symmetric magnets, using symmetry arguments and band structure calculations.
result: They uncover a Kramers dichroism effect where light selectively polarizes Kramers partnered states, allowing control of the internal degree of freedom.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for optical control in magnetic materials, but it is not relevant to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Non-normal Eigenvector Amplification In Multidimensional Kesten Processes
authors: Virgile Troude And Didier Sornette
abstract:

Heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics pervade physics, finance, and economics, yet their origin is often ascribed to systems poised near criticality. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033050] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that heavy-tailed fluctuations can arise from non-normal eigenvector amplification in multidimensional Kesten processes, far from criticality.
motivation: To explain the origin of heavy-tailed statistics in complex systems without invoking criticality.
method: Analyzes a multidimensional Kesten process and demonstrates non-normal eigenvector amplification as a mechanism for power-law distributions.
result: Heavy-tailed behavior emerges from non-normal amplification even when the system is stable, providing a universal mechanism.
conclusion: Non-normal eigenvector amplification is a generic route to heavy-tailed fluctuations, relevant to physics, finance, and economics.

title: Anisotropic Interactions Induce Dynamical Spin Freezing In Artificial Colloidal Ice
authors: Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú And Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033051] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical spin freezing in an artificial colloidal ice system with anisotropic interactions, focusing on frustration and real-time visualization.
motivation: To understand the effects of frustration in controlled environments by modifying artificial colloidal ice with anisotropic interactions.
method: The authors induce anisotropic interactions in an artificial colloidal ice system and observe the dynamics using optical visualization.
result: Anisotropic interactions lead to dynamical spin freezing, where the system exhibits arrested dynamics.
conclusion: The study provides insights into frustration and slow dynamics in artificial spin ice systems.

title: Ultracold Amplification Proposal For Parity Violation In Chiral Molecules
authors: Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, And Salvador Miret-Artés
abstract:

We propose a theoretical mechanism to indirectly detect the small parity-violating energy difference (PVED) between chiral enantiomers through a macroscopic enantiomeric excess observed in an ultracold gas.
