title: VaporISAC: Integrated Sensing And Communication Via Molecular Signals
authors: Sunasheer Bhattacharjee, Mart\'in Schottlender, Pit Hofmann, Juan A. Cabrera, Frank H. P. Fitzek, Falko Dressler
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional electromagnetic (EM)-based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems degrade in cluttered, obstructed, and radio-frequency-hostile environments, while macroscopic molecular communication (MC) remains largely unexplored as an ISAC medium. This article introduces VaporISAC, a molecular ISAC framework in which chemical vapor pulses simultaneously convey information and probe the propagation environment, enabling a one signal, two outputs paradigm. The same received waveform is jointly processed to recover transmitted information and infer environmental properties such as airflow, turbulence, smoke, and chemical conditions. Rather than replacing conventional EM-based ISAC, VaporISAC complements existing approaches in chemically dynamic, infrastructure-limited, and EM-challenged environments. The sensing principles, system architecture, proof-of-concept demonstrations, emerging applications, and open research challenges of VaporISAC are presented, positioning it as a promising new paradigm for resilient communication and environmental sensing.
tldr: This paper proposes a molecular communication framework for integrated sensing and communication using chemical vapor pulses.
motivation: Conventional EM-based ISAC systems fail in cluttered or RF-hostile environments; molecular communication offers a complementary approach.
method: Chemical vapor pulses are transmitted and the received waveform is jointly processed for information decoding and environmental sensing.
result: Proof-of-concept demonstrations show feasibility of simultaneous communication and sensing of airflow, turbulence, smoke, etc.
conclusion: VaporISAC is a promising new paradigm for resilient communication in chemically dynamic and infrastructure-limited environments.

title: Code-Poisoning Property Inference Attacks
authors: Xukun Luan, Yuhui Gong, Gang Zhang, Zixuan Huang, Yuanguo Bi, Xuesong Li, Jinyan Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The flourishing code hosting platforms and coding agents enable even beginners with private data to build tailored Machine Learning (ML) models using available code quickly. The training data for ML models, often regarded as private property (e.g., clinical records, transaction information), is at significant risk of information leakage. Property Inference Attacks (PIAs), as a significant type of privacy attack, aim to expose global property information of the training set. In this paper, we present Code-Poisoning Property Inference Attack (CPPIA), the first code-level PIA, which overcomes four limitations of existing works: insufficient attack performance, severe degradation of model accuracy, high computational overhead, and failure under defenses. We consider malicious code providers from code hosting platforms (GitHub) and coding agents (Codex). Upon downloading the poisoned code, data holders train models with their private data without professional auditing, subsequently releasing label-only APIs to the public. The adversary embeds the properties into secret samples during training and queries the trained model on these samples later to leak privacy. CPPIA offers 100\% attack accuracy without degrading model accuracy. It is also computationally lightweight and requires no shadow models. We evaluate the attack performance across four datasets, eight model architectures, eighteen properties, and under three defense mechanisms, demonstrating the universality and effectiveness of CPPIA.
tldr: This paper presents a code-level property inference attack that poisons training code to leak global properties of private training data.
motivation: Existing property inference attacks suffer from low accuracy, model degradation, high cost, and vulnerability to defenses; the authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: The adversary embeds properties into secret samples during training by providing poisoned code; after the victim trains a model, the adversary queries the model on these secret samples to infer properties.
result: CPPIA achieves 100% attack accuracy without degrading model accuracy, is computationally lightweight, and requires no shadow models.
conclusion: The attack is universal and effective across multiple datasets, architectures, properties, and defenses, highlighting a new privacy risk from code-level poisoning.

title: Reducing Power Consumption Of Embedded Dynamic Memories With ECCs
authors: Wenqing Song, Yifei Shen, Andreas Burg
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gain-cell embedded dynamic random-access memory (GCRAM) offers dense and energy-efficient on-chip storage, but retention-time variations force frequent refresh operations to cover worst-case bits. Error-correction codes (ECCs) can alleviate this limitation by masking bit errors from weak cells and thereby reduce refresh cost. However, the trade-off between the additional access and logic energy introduced by ECCs and the power savings from longer refresh intervals is nontrivial, especially considering the wide range of available ECC options. To optimize overall power consumption, we propose an ECC selection method that combines a refresh-interval model with power analysis to identify the minimum-power ECC configurations under a given yield constraint. Across different memory bandwidths, activity factors, and read/write ratios, the evaluation results show that the best ECC option shifts from stronger codes in refresh-dominated operating regions to lower-overhead codes in access-dominated regions and achieves 46.8% to 94.8% reduction in total power relative to the no-ECC reference.
tldr: This paper proposes an ECC selection method to reduce power consumption in embedded dynamic memories.
motivation: Gain-cell embedded DRAM suffers from retention-time variations requiring frequent refresh operations; ECCs can mask errors and reduce refresh cost, but the power trade-off is nontrivial.
method: The authors combine a refresh-interval model with power analysis to identify minimum-power ECC configurations under a yield constraint.
result: The best ECC option shifts from stronger codes in refresh-dominated regions to lower-overhead codes in access-dominated regions, achieving 46.8% to 94.8% total power reduction.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively optimizes power consumption in embedded memories by selecting appropriate ECCs based on operating conditions.

title: A Variable-Length Gray Code For The Natural Numbers
authors: Ezequiel L\'opez-Rubio
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reflected binary Gray code arranges the fixed-length binary representations of the integers so that consecutive numbers differ in a single bit. Its usefulness, however, is tied to a fixed word length [MATH], which both caps the range of representable numbers at [MATH] and wastes bits on small integers. We introduce a [MATH], a total function from the natural numbers to the set of all finite binary strings, obtained by taking the reflected Gray code of [MATH], discarding its leading zeros, and deleting the single leading one. We prove four properties of this construction. First, [MATH] is a bijection between the natural numbers and [MATH], so it is a complete code that assigns exactly one codeword to every finite binary string, including the empty string. Second, the Levenshtein (edit) distance between the codewords of two consecutive integers is always one; within a block of equal-length codewords the step is a single-bit substitution, and at each block boundary it is a single insertion. Third, codeword length is monotone non-decreasing in the encoded number and equals [MATH]. Fourth, the transition from [MATH]-bit to [MATH]-bit codewords occurs exactly at [MATH], where [MATH]. The code therefore realises a Hamiltonian enumeration of [MATH] under unit edit steps while retaining a near-optimal, self-adapting length profile. We discuss its compression behaviour relative to fixed-length Gray codes and its application to the family of instruction-set string encodings of graphs, hypergraphs, molecules and symbolic-regression expressions, in which the Levenshtein distance between encodings is used as a structural-similarity proxy.
tldr: This paper introduces a variable-length Gray code for natural numbers with unit Levenshtein distance between consecutive codewords.
motivation: Fixed-length Gray codes cap the range of representable numbers and waste bits on small integers; a variable-length code can adapt to the number size.
method: The code is constructed by taking the reflected binary Gray code of a number, discarding leading zeros, and deleting the leading one, then proving bijection, edit distance, length monotonicity, and transition properties.
result: The code is a bijection between natural numbers and all finite binary strings, with Levenshtein distance 1 between consecutive codewords, monotone non-decreasing length, and transitions at powers of two.
conclusion: The code offers a self-adapting length profile and potential applications in graph, hypergraph, molecule, and symbolic-regression encodings where edit distance proxies structural similarity.

title: Adaptive Fault Injection Planning For Multi-Layer Self-Healing Ai Infrastructure
authors: Saurabh Kulkarni, Yuxin Yang, Rohan Kulkarni, Gautam Nayak
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern GPU-accelerator platforms rely on multi-layer self-healing pipelines that span hardware, firmware, management software, and orchestration. When faults propagate across layer boundaries, they can bypass detection, corrupt diagnosis, or trigger conflicting remediations--yet conventional fault-injection campaigns test each layer in isolation. We present ADA-ST, an adaptive fault-injection methodology that uses a weighted fault-propagation graph to guide cross-layer scenario selection. We construct four-layer graphs for three successive platforms at a hyperscale operator: Alpha, Beta, and Gamma. Platform Alpha, a production system that accumulated 72,550 repair tickets over four years, provides the empirical foundation; 49% of those tickets involve cross-layer fault propagation. We show that existing static test campaigns cover only 20-25% of the modeled fault-propagation edges, leaving approximately three-quarters of the cross-layer attack surface unexercised. ADA-ST closes this gap through iterative, activity-guided scenario selection that maximizes marginal coverage gain per iteration, reaching full edge coverage within 10 iterations on Alpha, 12 on Beta, and 9 on Gamma. The Fault-Layer Abstraction Mapping (FLAM) transfers propagation knowledge across hardware generations with 100% fidelity from Alpha to Beta and 96% from Beta to Gamma. Physical spot-validation on the newest platform confirms all four tested propagation edges, revealing cross-layer vulnerabilities spanning telemetry blind spots, absence-based detection gaps, multi-signal correlation failures, and trust-without-verification propagation at the L2-to-L3 boundary.
tldr: This paper presents an adaptive fault injection methodology for multi-layer self-healing AI infrastructure, focusing on cross-layer fault propagation in GPU-accelerator platforms.
motivation: Conventional fault-injection campaigns test each layer in isolation, leaving cross-layer attack surfaces unexercised and vulnerabilities undetected.
method: ADA-ST uses a weighted fault-propagation graph to guide iterative scenario selection, maximizing marginal coverage gain per iteration, and employs Fault-Layer Abstraction Mapping (FLAM) to transfer knowledge across hardware generations.
result: ADA-ST achieves full edge coverage within 9-12 iterations on three platforms, compared to 20-25% coverage by static tests; FLAM transfers propagation knowledge with 96-100% fidelity.
conclusion: Adaptive, cross-layer fault injection is effective for uncovering vulnerabilities in multi-layer self-healing systems and can be transferred across hardware generations.

title: Ads-c: Antidistillation Sampling For Classification
authors: Mohammad Javad Khojasteh Khawaja Abaid Ullah
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15467v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowledge distillation enables an adversary to replicate a proprietary classifier by querying its prediction interface and training a surrogate on the returned probability vectors. Antidistillation sampling, proposed for large language models, counters this threat with an input-dependent, gradient-directed perturbation of the served distribution; its transfer to classification has not been studied. Adapting the defense to classification, we show its behavior is governed by the distribution of the teacher's per-input confidence margins. Because well-trained classifiers are severely overconfident, the direct transfer exhibits an inert window: below a closed-form-predictable threshold, it affects neither attacker nor defender; beyond it, the defense undergoes a phase transition and degrades the teacher faster than the attacker's student. Temperature softening rescales the transition in closed form, and every temperature configuration lies on the same unfavorable trade-off curve. Our method, ADS-C, composes the perturbation under a closed-form, per-input margin budget that provably preserves every served top-1 prediction, so the defended teacher's accuracy equals the undefended teacher's identically. Under this guarantee the distilled student still loses 17.4 percentage points on CIFAR-100, 29.6 on CIFAR-10, and 13.3 on Tiny-ImageNet; matching this degradation with the unmodified defense costs 27.5, 32.9, and 22.2 points of teacher accuracy. Because served labels are unchanged, a hard-label attacker gains nothing, while the defended soft output trains a student up to 29.7 points below that floor: the incentive to distill served probabilities is not merely removed but reversed. To our knowledge, ADS-C is the first antidistillation defense for classification whose utility cost is exactly zero.
tldr: This paper proposes ADS-C, an antidistillation defense for classification that perturbs softmax outputs to prevent knowledge distillation while preserving top-1 accuracy.
motivation: Knowledge distillation can be used by adversaries to replicate proprietary classifiers. Existing antidistillation defenses for LLMs have not been adapted to classification, and direct transfer suffers from an inert window and unfavorable trade-offs.
method: ADS-C applies a gradient-directed perturbation to the served probability distribution, with a closed-form per-input margin budget that guarantees unchanged top-1 predictions. Temperature softening is used to rescale the transition.
result: ADS-C reduces distilled student accuracy by up to 29.6 points on CIFAR-10 while maintaining teacher accuracy identical to the undefended model. Hard-label attackers gain nothing, and soft-label attackers are worse off.
conclusion: ADS-C is the first antidistillation defense for classification with zero utility cost, effectively removing the incentive to distill served probabilities.

title: Intentional Electromagnetic Interference Attacks On Facial Recognition
authors: Adam Czajka Tyler Fitzsimmons
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15512v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Attacks on general computer vision algorithms are often relegated to the digital domain, with the optimization performed purely in the digital world and then translated to physical mediums for implementation. In the field of biometrics, including facial recognition, physical presentation attacks targeting biometric sensors are dominant and present significant opportunity and risk. This paper highlights a critical vulnerability in the physical-to-digital pipeline of biometric sensors and provides a standardized approach for testing facial recognition system robustness against hardware attacks, going beyond and potentially complementing presentation attacks (as defined in ISO/IEC 30107 standard series). Specifically, in this work we (a) demonstrate that intentional electromagnetic interference is possible to be conducted with commonly accessible radio frequency (RF) equipment, (b) assess the robustness of state-of-the-art face recognition methods against RF-based attacks, and (c) provide a dataset composed of face images captured with and without electromagnetic interference to serve as a new benchmark for testing modern face matchers against RF-sourced interference.
tldr: This paper investigates intentional electromagnetic interference attacks on facial recognition systems, demonstrating vulnerabilities in the physical-to-digital pipeline.
motivation: Facial recognition systems are vulnerable to hardware attacks beyond digital domain; electromagnetic interference can disrupt sensor operation.
method: The authors use commonly accessible RF equipment to generate electromagnetic interference and capture face images under attack, then test state-of-the-art face matchers.
result: They show that electromagnetic interference can degrade facial recognition performance and provide a benchmark dataset.
conclusion: Hardware attacks via electromagnetic interference pose a realistic threat to biometric systems, and standardized testing is needed.

title: Publicly-Verifiable Certificates For Statistical Algorithms
authors: Michael P. Kim Michael Ngo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Following Goldwasser, Rothblum, Shafer, and Yehudayoff, who defined a framework for interactive proofs of learning [ITCS'21], we initiate the study of non-interactive proofs of learning. We define and study a new notion: Publicly-Verifiable Certificates of Statistical Validity (pvCSVs), which allow for public, distributionally-robust certification that the result of a learning algorithm is valid. In a pvCSV, a learner publishes a hypothesis [MATH] and corresponding certificate [MATH]; then, any user, who holds a user-specific distribution, can read the pair [MATH] and determine efficiently whether the hypothesis is valid according to the user-specific distribution. We construct pvCSVs in the context of Adaptive Statistical Query (SQ) Algorithms. To certify SQ algorithms that makes [MATH] adaptive queries, we construct pvCSVs where the sample complexity scales with [MATH], whereas the sample complexity of the best learning algorithms scale with [MATH]. More generally, we study proof systems for learning in the SQ model, demonstrating the model's strengths as well as its limitations.
tldr: This paper introduces publicly-verifiable certificates for statistical validity of learning algorithms in the SQ model, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To enable non-interactive, distributionally-robust certification of learning algorithm outputs, extending interactive proofs of learning.
method: Defines pvCSVs and constructs them for adaptive SQ algorithms, analyzing sample complexity trade-offs.
result: Constructs pvCSVs with sample complexity scaling with the number of adaptive queries, while learning algorithms scale with the number of queries.
conclusion: The work provides a proof system for learning in the SQ model, highlighting its strengths and limitations.

title: DFT-p-FDMA Based Chirp Transmission In Cp-ofdm For Unified Isac Waveform Design
authors: Fabrizio Carpi, Joonyoung Cho, Kyeong Jin Kim, Charlie Jianzhong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose an integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) framework that supports chirp signal transmission in CP-OFDM-based multiple access communication systems, enabling efficient coexistence of communication and sensing capabilities. Our framework employs the discrete Fourier transform phase rotated and permuted frequency division multiple access (DFT-p-FDMA) waveform to transmit chirp signals using a portion of the frequency resources, while ensuring interference-free concurrent CP-OFDM data transmissions on other bands. We analyze the effective channel behavior under the DFT-p-FDMA waveform, characterizing how delays and Doppler shifts impact radar target echoes. We also show how processing multiple received symbols improves Doppler resolution in practical scenarios. Our framework allows flexible adjustment of range-Doppler resolution through optimized time-frequency resource allocation, offering a versatile solution for ISAC applications. Simulation results validate the framework's performance in delay and Doppler estimation, highlighting its potential to support ISAC in next-generation wireless networks.
tldr: This paper proposes an ISAC framework using DFT-p-FDMA for chirp transmission in CP-OFDM, focusing on radar sensing and communication coexistence.
motivation: To enable efficient integration of sensing and communication in next-generation wireless networks by allowing chirp signals in CP-OFDM without interference.
method: The framework uses DFT-p-FDMA to allocate frequency resources for chirp signals while maintaining concurrent CP-OFDM data transmissions, and analyzes channel behavior for radar echoes.
result: Simulations validate the framework's performance in delay and Doppler estimation, showing flexible range-Doppler resolution through resource allocation.
conclusion: The proposed ISAC framework offers a versatile solution for next-generation wireless networks, but is not related to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition, history, and recent developments of active matter, including nonreciprocal interactions and quantum active matter.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is often used ambiguously; the paper aims to clarify its meaning and scope.
method: The authors review the history of the field, propose a definition of active matter as a subset of nonequilibrium systems, and survey recent developments.
result: They offer a clear definition and highlight emerging topics such as nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.
conclusion: Active matter is a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems, and the field is expanding into new areas including quantum systems.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using a scanning probe as an optical antenna.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with optical fluorescence, using the tip as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field at the tip apex.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for atomic-scale optical imaging and spectroscopy of molecules.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics and chemistry of transplutonium compounds under high pressure, focusing on their electronic structure and material properties.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique localized/itinerant behavior under pressure.
method: The paper is a review summarizing experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: It highlights the challenges and progress in understanding the behavior of these radioactive materials, including pressure-induced phase transitions and electronic changes.
conclusion: The review expands understanding of transplutonium materials but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and the implications for multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications of multimessenger observations for understanding physical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star physics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is the Nobel lecture on Boltzmann machines, a classical machine learning model, with no direct connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The lecture presents the development and significance of Boltzmann machines in machine learning.
method: The paper describes the architecture and learning algorithm of Boltzmann machines.
result: Boltzmann machines are a class of stochastic neural networks capable of learning complex probability distributions.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines have been influential in machine learning but are not related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three complementary real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture of defects.
result: The review highlights how each technique provides unique information about disorder and how combining them yields a more comprehensive understanding.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques, especially when combined, are powerful tools for characterizing atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the quantum physics of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, but direct measurements are often impossible due to extremely small reaction rates.
method: The authors summarize the state-of-the-art theoretical framework for low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discuss new experimental approaches.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of the quantum-mechanical phenomena governing stellar nuclear reactions and outlines current theoretical and experimental challenges.
conclusion: The paper concludes that further theoretical and experimental advances are needed to accurately model stellar nuclear reactions, which are essential for astrophysics.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, and periodic updates incorporate new measurements and improve precision.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, taking into account correlations and uncertainties.
result: A self-consistent set of values and uncertainties for over 300 constants and conversion factors is provided.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values represent the best available estimates and are recommended for use in research and applications.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review covers the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: The paper summarizes the state of the art in optoacoustic microscopy and its applications.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological imaging, but it does not relate to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory applied to buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the formation of wrinkles, creases, and cusps in soft materials under compression or growth is important for materials science and biology.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.
result: It provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and related phenomena in nonlinear elasticity.
conclusion: The paper is a comprehensive review of mechanical instabilities in soft matter, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Machine-learning-enabled Solvent Engineering For Uniform Quantum Dot Packing In Efficient And Stable Quantum-dot Light-emitting Diodes
authors: Beomsoo Chun, Byong Jae Kim, Hyeongjin Kim, Jeong Han Song, Yeongsik Kim, Jaehoon Lim And Jeonghun Kwak
abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) offer size-tunable optoelectronic properties and solution processability, yet achieving uniformly packed emissive layers remains a bottleneck for high-performance quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). Here, we report a machine learning -guided solvent optimization strategy to produce homogeneous QD films. Five representative solvent parameters are evaluated, and multiple regression models are trained against film uniformity derived from atomic force microscopy. Among them, support vector regression provides the highest predictive accuracy for film homogeneity. Guided by these predictions, we formulate a mixed solvent that closely matches the target profile, yielding superior packing homogeneity, which is confirmed by grazing-incidence small-angle x-ray scattering. QLEDs fabricated with this formulation exhibit an external quantum efficiency of 20.6% and an operational lifetime of 468.5 h at 20 000 cd m−2, surpassing all single-solvent controls. These findings establish packing homogeneity as a decisive factor for device performance and introduce a generalizable and scalable framework for data-driven design of solution-processed devices, holding strong potential for next-generation optoelectronic systems.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to optimize solvent mixtures for uniform quantum dot packing in QLEDs, achieving high efficiency and long lifetime.
motivation: Achieving uniformly packed emissive layers is a bottleneck for high-performance quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs).
method: Five solvent parameters were evaluated, and multiple regression models (with support vector regression best) were trained to predict film uniformity from atomic force microscopy data, guiding the formulation of a mixed solvent.
result: The optimized solvent yielded superior packing homogeneity, and QLEDs achieved 20.6% external quantum efficiency and 468.5 h operational lifetime at 20,000 cd/m².
conclusion: Packing homogeneity is a decisive factor for device performance, and the data-driven framework is generalizable for solution-processed devices.

title: Probing Anharmonic And Heterogeneous Carrier Dynamics Across Sublattice Melting In A Minimal Model Superionic Conductor
authors: Sucharita Niyogitakenobu Nakamuragenki Kobayashiyasunobu Andotakeshi Kawasakiahttps://ror.org/035t8zc32large-Scale Computational Science Research Division, D3 Center, The University Of Osaka, Toyonaka 560–0043, Japanbhttps://ror.org/035t8zc32department Of Physics, The University Of Osaka, Osaka 560–0043, Japanchttps://ror.org/04chrp450department Of Physics, Nagoya University, Nagoya 464–8601, Japandhttps://ror.org/01703db54department Of Materials And Chemistry Materials DX Research Center, National Institute Of Advanced Industrial Science And Technology, Ibaraki 305–8568, Japanesolid State Chemistry Laboratory, Pioneering Research Institute (PRI), RIKEN, Saitama 351–0198, Japanfhttps://ror.org/05dqf9946institute Of Integrated Research, Institute Of Science Tokyo, Kanagawa 226–8501, Japan

tldr: This paper studies carrier dynamics and sublattice melting in a model superionic conductor using computational methods.
motivation: To understand the microscopic mechanism of liquid-like ionic transport in superionic conductors while the lattice remains solid.
method: The authors use a simple, chemically neutral model and computational simulations to probe anharmonic and heterogeneous carrier dynamics across sublattice melting.
result: They identify the emergence of liquid-like ionic transport and characterize the associated carrier dynamics.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the fundamental physics of superionic conduction, but the work is focused on materials science and condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Ramanujan Srinathyunlong Xudouglas A. Ruffamy M. Nibrent Doironmarlene R. SignificanceThe brain must continually decide which aspects of sensory information are relevant for current goals while ignoring others. We found that the shared trial-to-trial variability of visual neurons identifies the sensory information that is most ...
tldr: This paper studies how correlated variability in sensory neurons reflects task-relevant information, focusing on neural coding in visual cortex.
motivation: Understanding how the brain extracts relevant sensory information amidst noise is fundamental to neuroscience, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze trial-to-trial variability in visual neurons and relate it to task-relevant information using statistical models.
result: They find that the structure of correlated variability is shaped by the behavioral relevance of stimuli, indicating efficient coding.
conclusion: The study provides insights into neural computation but is unrelated to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Loss Of Positive Definiteness Is A Symptom, Not The Cause, Of high-Weissenberg-number Breakdown
authors: Yuan Yu, Lanjin Lian, Feiyang Chu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Numerical breakdown at high Weissenberg number is often attributed to loss of symmetric positive definiteness (SPD) of the conformation tensor. That conclusion follows from Maxwell-type models without solvent viscosity. With solvent fraction [MATH], the initial-value problem is locally well posed for arbitrary symmetric stress. We derive the missing quantitative theory for indefinite states and test its computational consequences. Frozen-coefficient analysis gives a growth rate uniformly bounded in wavenumber and the direction-resolved instability threshold [MATH]; stress diffusion supplies a closed-form cutoff, while the classical [MATH] catastrophe is recovered as solvent viscosity vanishes. A determinant identity shows that violations self-heal on the timescale [MATH], so persistent violations measure the truncation error that recreates them. Spectral and lattice Boltzmann tests reproduce the threshold, solvent-fraction reversal, and resolution independence. In four-roll-mill interventions, enforcing SPD delays blow-up by 15 convective times but reduces the stagnation-point Weissenberg number by 30%. Across five coupling schemes, a local second-moment stress source remains stable through the full budget at [MATH] while carrying [MATH]; the divergence-coupled variant fails at [MATH]. The surviving scheme matches published benchmarks within 0.05% and 0.18% at [MATH] and 20. Thus loss of positive definiteness is neither necessary nor sufficient for breakdown: the discrete coupling route decides, and the violation is a resolution gauge for which we provide run-time monitors.
tldr: This paper investigates numerical breakdown in high-Weissenberg-number flows of viscoelastic fluids, showing that loss of positive definiteness of the conformation tensor is neither necessary nor sufficient for breakdown.
motivation: Numerical simulations of viscoelastic fluids at high Weissenberg number often fail, and the cause has been attributed to loss of symmetric positive definiteness (SPD) of the conformation tensor. The authors aim to clarify the true mechanism.
method: The authors derive a quantitative theory for indefinite states using frozen-coefficient analysis, derive a determinant identity showing self-healing of violations, and test their predictions with spectral and lattice Boltzmann simulations.
result: They find that loss of SPD is neither necessary nor sufficient for breakdown; the discrete coupling scheme determines stability. They provide a closed-form cutoff for stress diffusion and run-time monitors for violations.
conclusion: The breakdown at high Weissenberg number is not caused by loss of positive definiteness but by the choice of numerical coupling scheme; the violation serves as a resolution gauge.

title: An Exact N-strain Epidemic Model Using Bond Percolation
authors: Peter Mann, V. Anne Smith, John B. O. Mitchell, Simon Dobson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we examine the emergent structures of random networks that have undergone bond percolation an arbitrary, but finite, number of times. We define two types of sequential branching processes: a competitive branching process - in which each iteration performs bond percolation on the residual graph (RG) resulting from previous generations; and, a collaborative branching process - where percolation is performed on the giant connected component (GCC) instead. We investigate the behaviour of these models, including the expected size of the GCC for a given generation, the critical percolation probability and other topological properties of the resulting graph structures using the analytically exact method of generating functions. We explore this model for Erdos-Renyi and scale free random graphs. This model can be interpreted as a seasonal N-strain model of disease spreading.
tldr: This paper uses bond percolation on random graphs to model N-strain epidemic spreading, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand emergent structures in networks after multiple rounds of bond percolation, motivated by modeling seasonal multi-strain disease dynamics.
method: They define competitive and collaborative branching processes on residual graphs and giant components, and use generating functions to analytically compute properties like GCC size and percolation thresholds for Erdős–Rényi and scale-free graphs.
result: Exact expressions for expected GCC size and critical percolation probability are derived for sequential percolation, revealing differences between competitive and collaborative processes.
conclusion: The model provides a framework for N-strain epidemic modeling but remains purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-Gaussianity In Cat Codes: Global Incompatibility And Local Geometric Alignment With The Magic Resource
authors: Yuwei Zhu, Seungbeom Chin, William J. Munro, Kae Nemoto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Gaussianity is an essential resource for genuine quantum advantages in continuous-variable quantum systems and is regarded as a counterpart of the magic resource in discrete-variable systems. Recently, an exact correspondence between non-Gaussianity (NG) and the magic resource was identified within the Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) encoding framework. Whether such a relation persists beyond GKP encoding, however, remains unclear. Here, we address this question in the cat-code setting. By comparing the Wigner logarithmic negativity (WLN) and a magic measure defined from a phase-operator basis, we analyze the resource geometry of non-degenerate [MATH]-peaked cat states. We find that cat codes do not inherit the global value-preserving GKP magic--NG equivalence, but their asymptotic WLN geometry allows a constructive local alignment with the magic-measure geometry. Specifically, under a distinguished SU([MATH]) asymptotic cat code, we establish a sector-dependent alignment between WLN level sets and magic-measure level sets based on their intrinsic local geometries. These results identify both the global incompatibility and the locally constructive relation between magic and non-Gaussian resources in cat codes, suggesting a geometry-based approach to resource correspondences beyond the GKP framework.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Triple-Resonance Spectroscopy Using A Cavity-Enhanced Frequency Comb Probe
authors: Qinxue Nie, Vinicius Silva de Oliveira, Adrian Hj\"alt\'en, Isak Silander, Kevin K. Lehmann, Aleksandra Foltynowicz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate experimentally verified models of molecular hot-band transitions are essential for interpreting high-temperature spectra in environments ranging from exoplanetary atmospheres to combustion systems. However, line-resolved measurements of infrared hot-band transitions reaching highly excited vibrational states above 10000 cm[MATH] are missing because these transitions are too weak to observe at room temperature and become spectrally congested at elevated temperatures. Here, we introduce a nonlinear spectroscopic approach that enables simultaneous measurement of individual infrared hot-band transitions between four vibrational bands up to 12000 cm[MATH] over a broad spectral range with sub-Doppler resolution and sub-MHz frequency accuracy (10[MATH] relative line position accuracy). The methods is based on an all-optical triple-resonance (AOTR) scheme that combines stepwise mid-infrared pumping using an optical-frequency-comb-stabilized, double-seeded continuous-wave optical parametric oscillator with broadband highly sensitive near-infrared probing using a cavity-enhanced optical frequency comb. As a proof of principle, we measure transitions between high polyads (P) of methane - groups of strongly interacting, near-degenerate vibrational energy states arising from couplings between the C-H stretching and bending modes. In a single probe spectrum, we simultaneously resolve sub-Doppler P4[MATH]P0, P6[MATH]P2 and P8[MATH]P4 transitions, reaching the poorly understood polyad P8 near 12000 cm[MATH] and providing the first set of 41 experimentally observed lines in the P8[MATH]P4 spectral region.Comb-based AOTR spectroscopy opens a new route for broadband exploration of highly excited molecular states, delivering extensive high-accuracy spectroscopic data needed to refine molecular models and improve predictions of high-temperature spectra.
tldr: This paper presents a novel triple-resonance spectroscopy technique using a cavity-enhanced frequency comb probe to measure infrared hot-band transitions in methane with high resolution and accuracy.
motivation: Accurate models of molecular hot-band transitions are needed for interpreting high-temperature spectra in exoplanetary atmospheres and combustion systems, but line-resolved measurements of highly excited vibrational states are missing due to weak signals and spectral congestion.
method: The method uses an all-optical triple-resonance scheme combining stepwise mid-infrared pumping with a double-seeded continuous-wave OPO stabilized by an optical frequency comb, and broadband near-infrared probing with a cavity-enhanced frequency comb.
result: The technique simultaneously resolves sub-Doppler transitions between high polyads of methane (P4→P0, P6→P2, P8→P4) up to 12000 cm⁻¹, providing the first 41 experimentally observed lines in the P8→P4 region.
conclusion: Comb-based AOTR spectroscopy enables broadband exploration of highly excited molecular states, delivering high-accuracy spectroscopic data to refine molecular models and improve predictions of high-temperature spectra.

title: Metric Tensors And Two-forms In Information Geometry From The Gns Construction
authors: M. Castrill\'on L\'opez, F. M. Ciaglia, L. Gonz\'alez-Bravo, A. Ibort
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a GNS-based construction of geometric tensors on smooth parametric statistical models over [MATH]-algebras. Since the state space of a [MATH]-algebra is generally not a smooth manifold, the construction does not rely on pulling back tensors from an ambient state manifold. Instead, the GNS Hilbert spaces and their duals are organized into non-locally-trivial Hilbert fibrations over the state space. For models satisfying a compatibility condition expressing derivatives of expectation values as continuous functionals on the realified GNS fibers, each tangent vector admits a canonical dual GNS representative. Pulling back the dual GNS Hermitian product along the corresponding canonical lift produces a Hermitian tensor [MATH] on the complexified tangent bundle of the model, whose real and imaginary parts define, under suitable regularity assumptions, a smooth weak Riemannian metric tensor [MATH] and a smooth two-form [MATH]. In finite-dimensional parameter manifolds the metric is, of course, strong. The construction recovers the Fisher--Rao metric in the commutative dominated case, the Fubini--Study geometry for pure states up to the normalization and sign convention imposed by the dual GNS pairing, and the SLD metric for faithful quantum states. In finite-dimensional faithful models, the two-form [MATH] is proportional, up to convention, to the expected commutator of the SLD representatives, equivalently to the mean Uhlmann curvature. We show through faithful qubits and displaced thermal states that [MATH] need not be closed. For bundle-regular models, the associated fiberwise symplectic form on the real dual GNS bundle admits connection-dependent closed extensions to the total space, while closedness of [MATH] on the parameter manifold is controlled by the covariant exterior derivative of the canonical real dual GNS lift.

title: Conjugate Phase-noise Cancellation Enables Submicrometre Dual-comb Ranging With Free-running Megahertz-linewidth Lasers
authors: Yue You, Zaifan Wu, Yi Zou, Xiang Cai, Yixiao Zhu, Chenbo Zhang, Dan Lu, Siming Chen, Shujie Pan, Xian Zhou, Xiaopeng Xie, Fan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frequency-domain dual-comb ranging combines rapid acquisition with interferometric sensitivity, but high-performance implementations often rely on mutually coherent or actively stabilised comb sources. Free-running sources can reduce this hardware burden, but their phase noise and drift of the optical frequency offset can blur radio-frequency (RF) comb teeth and weaken probe-reference phase correlation. Previous phase-slope implementations have therefore relied on sufficiently resolved RF teeth, within-coherence-length probe-reference paths or explicit digital tracking of these fluctuations. Here we demonstrate a low-cost frequency-domain dual-comb ranging architecture that combines independent free-running distributed-feedback (DFB) lasers with conjugate phase-noise cancellation (CPNC). By forming a self-conjugate signal before the phases of individual RF-comb teeth are extracted, CPNC cancels the common laser phase factor and drifting optical-frequency-offset term while retaining the distance-dependent phase slope. Using electro-optic combs seeded by DFB lasers with linewidths of 12 MHz and 9 MHz, we achieve an Allan deviation of [MATH] at [MATH] and reduce the single-frame distance standard deviation from [MATH] to [MATH] with CPNC. Across the tested megahertz-linewidth configurations, CPNC delivered minimum Allan deviations below [MATH]. These results show that CPNC enables submicrometre ranging in a low-cost frequency-domain dual-comb architecture with reduced source-stabilisation and phase-management complexity.
tldr: This paper presents a dual-comb ranging technique using free-running lasers with conjugate phase-noise cancellation to achieve submicrometer precision.
motivation: High-performance dual-comb ranging typically requires mutually coherent or actively stabilized comb sources, which are costly and complex. The authors aim to achieve submicrometer ranging with low-cost, free-running lasers.
method: They propose a conjugate phase-noise cancellation (CPNC) architecture that forms a self-conjugate signal before extracting phases of individual RF comb teeth, canceling common laser phase noise and optical frequency drift while preserving the distance-dependent phase slope.
result: Using electro-optic combs seeded by DFB lasers with 12 MHz and 9 MHz linewidths, they achieve an Allan deviation below 10^-7 at 1 ms and reduce single-frame distance standard deviation from 1.2 μm to 0.3 μm with CPNC.
conclusion: CPNC enables submicrometer ranging in a low-cost frequency-domain dual-comb architecture with reduced source-stabilization and phase-management complexity.

title: A persistent-homology-Gaussian Prior For Solving Infinite-dimensional Bayesian Inverse Scattering Problems
authors: Zhiyuan Wang, Hang Qi, Xiaofei Guan, Zhiliang Deng, Xiaomei Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian inference methods have been developed to address inverse problems in function spaces where the unknown parameters are of infinite dimension. However, conventional Gaussian priors remain inadequate for reconstructing discontinuous or sharply varying target functions encountered in practical applications like obstacle reconstruction. Although hybrid priors have emerged as a promising solution, significant challenges remain in developing theoretically rigorous and computationally tractable frameworks in engineering applications. To address these issues, we propose a persistent-homology-Gaussian (PHG) prior for solving the acoustic obstacle scattering inverse problem in the infinite-dimensional Bayesian setting, which combines a weighted persistence-based regularization term with a periodic Gaussian reference measure through a Gibbs tilt. Then, the complex boundary is represented by a log-radial function on the unit circle, so that the reconstruction from far-field data is formulated as a function-space inverse problem. The well-posedness of the resulting posterior measure is established in the Hellinger, total variation, and Wasserstein-\(p\) metrics. Furthermore, the convergence of finite-dimensional posterior approximations is obtained, and posterior sampling is performed by a preconditioned Crank--Nicolson (pCN) method. Numerical experiments show that the proposed PHG prior yields accurate and stable reconstructions under more extensive noisy conditions, providing explicit control of multiscale topological features and better performance compared to other conventional priors.
tldr: This paper proposes a persistent-homology-Gaussian prior for Bayesian inverse scattering problems, focusing on acoustic obstacle reconstruction.
motivation: Conventional Gaussian priors fail to reconstruct discontinuous or sharply varying target functions in inverse problems like obstacle reconstruction.
method: A persistent-homology-Gaussian prior combines a weighted persistence-based regularization term with a periodic Gaussian reference measure via Gibbs tilt, and posterior sampling uses a preconditioned Crank-Nicolson method.
result: The posterior measure is well-posed in Hellinger, total variation, and Wasserstein-p metrics, and numerical experiments show accurate and stable reconstructions under noisy conditions.
conclusion: The PHG prior provides explicit control of multiscale topological features and outperforms conventional priors for acoustic obstacle scattering inverse problems.

title: An FFT-Based Direct Splitting Method For Efficient Micromagnetic Simulations
authors: Hang Qi, Changqing Ye, Xiaofei Guan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation poses significant challenges for numerical simulation due to its nonlinearity, nonconvex unit-length constraint, and nonlocal field contributions. Existing implicit or semi-implicit schemes exhibit unconditional stability but require repeated solution of nonlinear or linearized systems, resulting in high computational costs. In this work, we revisit the tangent plane formulation and show that the resulting discrete problem at each time step can be written as a generalized saddle-point system. Exploiting this structure, we develop a matrix-free preconditioner for the implicit Euler scheme by combining FFT-based techniques with a splitting iteration method. We show that each component in the splitting method can be efficiently implemented in a direct fashion via fast Poisson solvers, enabling the design of an efficient preconditioner for iterative solvers. To enhance geometric consistency of the tangent vector and reduce projection steps, a Crank--Nicolson scheme is further investigated, retaining the same algorithmic structure as the Euler scheme, thus allowing direct reuse of preconditioners and solvers. Extensive 2D and 3D numerical experiments are conducted to validate the framework, demonstrating accurate constraint preservation, improved computational efficiency, and robust solver performance. The proposed approach is shown to scale effectively for large-scale micromagnetic simulations, making it suitable for practical applications in complex magnetic systems.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient numerical method for micromagnetic simulations using FFT-based direct splitting.
motivation: Micromagnetic simulations are computationally expensive due to the nonlinearity and nonlocal nature of the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.
method: The authors reformulate the tangent plane method as a generalized saddle-point system and develop a matrix-free preconditioner combining FFT and splitting iteration.
result: The method achieves accurate constraint preservation, improved efficiency, and robust performance in 2D and 3D tests.
conclusion: The proposed approach scales effectively for large-scale micromagnetic simulations, making it suitable for practical applications.

title: A 3d-aca Accelerated Time Domain Boundary Element Method For Elastodynamics Using Fmm And $\mathcal{H}$-matrix Techniques
authors: Martin Schanz Vibudha Lakshmi Keshava
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The time-domain Boundary Element Method (BEM) for linear elastodynamics with vanishing initial conditions is considered. Spatial discretization uses standard low-order boundary elements, while temporal discretization employs the generalized Convolution Quadrature (gCQ) method. The gCQ framework requires evaluating BEM matrices in the Laplace domain at several complex frequencies along a chosen contour, producing a three-dimensional tensor with one spatial matrix slice per frequency. To reduce storage and computational cost, a low rank approximation of the tensor is computed using 3D-Adaptive Cross Approximation (3D-ACA), extending the classical ACA to handle both the additional frequency dimension and the tensorial structure of elastodynamics. Within each frequency slice, the BEM matrices are further compressed using either the classical ACA algorithm using the [MATH]-matrix approach or a Chebyshev interpolation based Fast Multipole Method (FMM). A comparative study of all proposed methods is carried out using two academic examples, and the structural vibration of an induction machine is analyzed.
tldr: This paper presents a 3D-ACA accelerated time-domain boundary element method for elastodynamics using FMM and H-matrix techniques.
motivation: The time-domain BEM for elastodynamics is computationally expensive due to the need to evaluate matrices at many complex frequencies. The authors aim to reduce storage and computational cost.
method: They use 3D-Adaptive Cross Approximation (3D-ACA) to compress the tensor of BEM matrices across frequencies, and within each frequency slice, further compress using ACA with H-matrix or Chebyshev interpolation based FMM.
result: The proposed methods are compared on two academic examples and the structural vibration of an induction machine, demonstrating efficiency gains.
conclusion: The 3D-ACA accelerated BEM is effective for elastodynamics, but the work is purely computational mechanics with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: From A Windowed Square Wave To The Hyperbolic Tangent, Even Zeta Values, And Dirichlet L-Values
authors: Peter Bevelacqua
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We window a delayed periodic square wave with a decaying signum function and evaluate the product at zero frequency in both the time and frequency domains. The window renders every series that appears absolutely convergent, so the argument requires only elementary integrals and a limit. We obtain new unified derivations for the Mittag-Leffler partial-fraction expansion for the hyperbolic tangent, the Fourier expansion of the first Euler polynomial E1, and the Basel sum, zeta(2). The same calculation, followed by termwise integration, yields the Dirichlet beta value beta(3) = pi^3/32, and the values at s = 3 of two other Dirichlet L-functions. Termwise integration of this sine series produces zeta(4), and an induction continues the process to zeta(2k) for every k greater than or equal to 1.
tldr: This paper derives classical number theory results (zeta values, Dirichlet L-values) using elementary Fourier analysis of a windowed square wave.
motivation: To provide unified derivations of known results like the Basel sum and Dirichlet beta values using simple integrals and limits.
method: Windows a delayed periodic square wave with a decaying signum function, evaluates at zero frequency in time and frequency domains, and performs termwise integration.
result: Obtains Mittag-Leffler expansion for tanh, Fourier expansion of Euler polynomial E1, Basel sum ζ(2), Dirichlet beta β(3)=π^3/32, and ζ(2k) for all k≥1.
conclusion: The approach yields elementary derivations of several classical results in number theory and special functions.

title: Abel-Type Transformations And Telescoping Structures In Reciprocal Series Of Second-Order Linear Recurrences
authors: Kunle Adegoke, Robert Frontczak, Taras Goy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified method for transforming and evaluating infinite series involving products of terms of second-order linear recurrences in the denominator. These formulas provide a systematic framework that unifies and extends many known identities for Fibonacci and Lucas numbers. In addition, the method leads to explicit evaluations and identities involving several classical combinatorial sequences, including Catalan numbers, harmonic numbers, and Stirling numbers of both kinds. A key feature of the approach is that it naturally distinguishes between even and odd values of the parameter [MATH], leading to structurally different representations. The results show that summation by parts is an effective and flexible tool for reducing multi-factor reciprocal sums to simpler forms.

motivation: To provide a systematic framework for evaluating reciprocal series of second-order linear recurrences, unifying and extending known identities for Fibonacci and Lucas numbers.
method: The approach uses a discrete Abel-type summation formula (summation by parts) to convert reciprocal series with multiple factors into expressions with partial telescoping structure.

conclusion: Summation by parts is an effective tool for reducing multi-factor reciprocal sums to simpler forms, with structurally different representations for even and odd parameter values.

title: On The Computational Complexity Of Bilevel Integer Linear Programming
authors: Margarida Carvalho Nagisa Sugishita
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the computational complexity of bilevel integer linear programming. While Jeroslow~(1985) established that the decision version of this problem is [MATH]-complete when restricted to binary variables, we prove that this [MATH]-completeness persists even for general integer variables, settling a question that remained open for over 40 years. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of various structural assumptions on computational complexity. Notably, we strengthen the result of K\"oppe et al.~(2010) by proving polynomial-time solvability whenever the total number of upper- and lower-level variables is fixed, without any additional assumptions.

motivation: Bilevel integer linear programming is a fundamental optimization problem with applications in economics and engineering, but its computational complexity for general integer variables was unknown for over 40 years.
method: The authors use reductions from known Σ^p_2-complete problems and analyze structural assumptions to derive complexity results.
result: They prove Σ^p_2-completeness for general integer variables and show polynomial-time solvability when the total number of variables is fixed.
conclusion: The results settle a long-standing open question and provide a clear complexity landscape for bilevel integer linear programming.

title: Tropical Bi-Objective Pseudolinear Optimization As Parametric Mean-Payoff Games
authors: Ibrahim Hassan, Abdulhadi Aminu, Lawal Muhammad
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the parametric mean-payoff game framework of Parsons et al. to bi-objective tropical pseudolinear optimization with general two-sided constraints. The problem is to simultaneously minimize two tropical pseudolinear objectives over the feasible set of a general two-sided system U otimes x oplus b is less than or equal to V otimes x oplus d, we characterize the Pareto front via a parametric mean-payoff game in two parameters ( lambda 1, lambda 2). The feasibility region R is convex and the Pareto front P is a convex piecewise-linear curve with finitely many breakpoints, these properties are natural extensions of the single-parameter case to two parameters. In addition, we give as a new result, the joint denominator bound: the cycle coefficients satisfy k 1( gamma ) + k 2( gamma ) is less than or equal to 2 for any elementary cycle gamma, yielding | Delta | is less than or equal to 2 for every 2 times 2 Newton system, except in the fully decoupled case, and implying that all breakpoints have half-integer coordinates for integer data. Optimality and infeasibility certificates are given in terms of the cycle structure of the parametric game. Two algorithms are developed, a directional bisection algorithm (O(n squared (n+m) log M) per direction) and a Newton scheme tracing the complete Pareto front via 2 times 2 linear solves in at most | S | steps, independent of M. The directional bisection algorithm is pseudo-polynomial in n, m and M. The Newton scheme is independent of M but requires up to |S| steps, where |S| is exponential in n. Lastly, we give numerical experiments on random instances to confirm the directional bisection complexity bound exactly; the Newton scheme's worst-case bound is not attained by random instances but is shown to be tight via explicit adversarial constructions.

method: They model the problem as a parametric mean-payoff game in two parameters, analyze cycle structure, and develop a directional bisection algorithm and a Newton scheme.
result: The Pareto front is a convex piecewise-linear curve with finitely many breakpoints; joint denominator bound yields half-integer coordinates for integer data.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical characterization and algorithms for bi-objective tropical optimization, with complexity bounds and numerical validation.

title: Fast And Scalable Caputo Fractional Gradient Descent Via Perturbation-Preserving Memory Compression
authors: Hwanseo Lee, Junseo Lee, Hyunju Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional gradient descent (FGD) incorporates long-range memory through Caputo-type operators and has been shown to improve stability in ill-conditioned and nonconvex optimization problems. Despite these advantages, its practical use remains limited, mainly due to the high computational cost of evaluating history-dependent convolutions, which scales quadratically with the number of iterations. In this paper, we focus on making Caputo-based optimization computationally viable without sacrificing its intrinsic memory structure. We begin by expressing the fractional descent direction as a discrete convolution over past gradients, which provides a unified view of the method. Based on this formulation, we introduce two complementary mechanisms to reduce the cost of the memory term. The first uses a sum-of-exponentials (SOE) approximation of the power-law kernel, leading to efficient recursive updates. The second approach, newly proposed in this paper as dyadic hierarchical discrete convolution (DHDC), compresses the gradient history through a multiscale aggregation strategy. Rather than treating these approximations as purely numerical accelerations, we interpret them as perturbations of the ideal Caputo operator. This viewpoint allows us to analyze how the compressed memory affects the optimization dynamics. Under standard [MATH]-strong convexity and [MATH]-smoothness assumptions, we show that the resulting method still exhibits monotone descent and linear convergence, provided that the approximation error remains controlled.
tldr: This paper proposes fast and scalable algorithms for Caputo fractional gradient descent using memory compression techniques.
motivation: Fractional gradient descent suffers from high computational cost due to history-dependent convolutions, limiting its practical use.
method: The authors express the fractional descent direction as a discrete convolution and introduce sum-of-exponentials approximation and dyadic hierarchical discrete convolution to compress gradient history.
result: Under standard convexity and smoothness assumptions, the compressed methods maintain monotone descent and linear convergence with controlled approximation error.
conclusion: The proposed techniques make Caputo-based optimization computationally viable without sacrificing its intrinsic memory structure.

title: RCLUPPr: A New Randomized CholeskyQR With Lu Preconditioning

In contrast to the existing RCLUPP in , which applies matrix sketching before LUPP decomposition, RCLUPPr places LUPP decomposition as a preconditioning step first, significantly reducing error propagation. Our analysis rigorously proves that RCLUPPr enjoys markedly better applicability to the ill-conditioned matrices than the existing CholeskyQR-type algorithms and remains stable and accurate in the mixed-precision arithmetic. conclusion: RCLUPPr is a practical and robust algorithm for QR decomposition of tall-skinny matrices, particularly effective for ill-conditioned problems and mixed-precision computing.

title: Smooth Projections Of Self-similar Measures

abstract: ArXiv:2607.15635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Furstenberg-type criterion for a given orthogonal projection of a self-similar measure to be absolutely continuous, with quantified regularity. title: Penalty-scaling Effects In Nonsymmetric Interior-penalty Dg Discretizations Of Viscous Rotating Shallow-water Equations

title: Constructing Far-from-equilibrium Patterns In A Cross-diffusion Vegetation-autotoxicity Model
authors: Annalisa Iuorio, Cinzia Soresina, Frits Veerman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using geometric singular perturbation theory, we construct stationary, periodic, front-type far-from-equilibrium patterns in a cross-diffusion model for plant growth under the influence of toxicity. title: Integer Quadratic Obstructions To The Local Controllability Of The Burgers Equation
authors: Thomas Perrin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.15735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Burgers equation with a scalar control acting through a fixed spatial profile, in a regime where the linearized system is not controllable. We show that these conditions are related to iterated Lie brackets. The proof relies on repeated integrations by parts in the quadratic expansion combined with nonlinear remainder estimates. tldr: This paper studies quadratic obstructions to local controllability of the Burgers equation, a topic in control theory of partial differential equations.
motivation: Understanding controllability of nonlinear PDEs like Burgers equation is important for control theory, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze quadratic expansions and iterated Lie brackets to derive obstructions quantified by negative Sobolev norms.
result: They identify conditions on the control profile leading to obstructions at arbitrary integer orders and construct profiles achieving these obstructions.
conclusion: The work contributes to controllability theory of PDEs but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: On The $(n,\aleph_0)$-Lineability Of Nowhere Differentiable Functions
